sheet-1.description: Sheet 1 covers the commercial centre of Red Bank at 50 feet to an inch, with the drawing turned a few degrees so that Broad Street runs nearly down the page. The main business blocks lie along Front Street, which is lettered West Front to the left of Broad Street and East Front to the right and rises toward the east. On the left of Broad Street the blocks between Front and White Streets hold brick stores in pink and frame buildings in yellow, among them the Broad St. Nat'l Bank, Peters Bldg., the New Liberty Hotel, the Register printing office, a laundry and a garage, with Emanuel Court cutting through the block. East of Broad Street the block between Front and Mechanic Streets is solidly built with stores, a fire department building and a laundry. Farther east stand the Globe Theatre, a hardware and furniture store, the Palace Theatre, a garage and, along Wharf Avenue, the Union Hotel, produce houses and a hay and feed store. West of the stores, between Front Street and the river, are the Sheridan Hotel, the Monmouth Hotel, a bowling alley, a bottling works, the Lyceum, the Monmouth Boat Club and the Red Bank Yacht Works with its boat building and machine shop, served by marine railways. The upper left of the sheet is the North Branch of the Shrewsbury River or Navesink River, with boat houses, the Merchant Steamboat Co. freight house, a coal bin and a marine storage shed on the water side. A heavy line in the upper left marks a bulkhead or dock line. The area south of Mechanic Street at the bottom right is blank and belongs to sheet 2, apart from the library stamp and scale bar.
notes: West Front and East Front are the modern West Front Street and East Front Street; Front Street meets Broad Street at a single junction.
Mechanic is the modern Mechanic Street; Wharf Avenue and Globe Court keep their names.
Emanuel Court is not in the OpenStreetMap street network.
The heavy line in the upper left is a bulkhead or dock line along the river, not a separate map part.
Red Bank business centre: Broad, East and West Front, Mechanic, White; river at top. 50 ft.
placenames: North Branch of Shrewsbury River or Navesink River

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the southern end of the Red Bank business district and the first residential blocks beyond it, at 50 feet to an inch with Broad Street running nearly down the page. Along Broad Street the west side between White and Monmouth Streets holds the post office, an ice cream factory, the Eisner Bldg., a New York Telephone building, the Western Union and Postal telegraph offices, a lodge hall, a library and plumbing and piano shops, with a motion picture house, automobile showrooms and a garage near Monmouth Street. South of Monmouth Street the west side turns residential, with the 1st M. E. Church, St. James R. C. Church and frame dwellings with automobile houses down to Peters Place. East of Broad Street the Red Bank Trust Co., the Second Nat'l Bank, a candy factory, ice cream factory, auto repairing shops and the Strand Theatre (moving pictures, 385 seats) stand between Mechanic, Wallace and Linden Place. Farther east the blocks along Wallace Street, Linden Place and Canal Street are small frame dwellings on deep lots, ending at Hudson Avenue on the right edge. The blank area at the top left, with the compass, lies north of White Street; the sheet joins sheet 1 along Mechanic Street at the top, sheet 3 along Canal Street and Peters Place at the bottom, and sheet 6 along the right edge. A library stamp and scale bar occupy the lower right.
notes: Peters Place, Linden Place, Canal, Clay Street, Wallace, White, Monmouth and Mechanic correspond to Peters Place, Linden Place, Canal Street, Clay Street, Wallace Street, White Street, Monmouth Street and Mechanic Street today.
The 1st M. E. Church and St. James R. C. Church stand on the west side of Broad Street south of Monmouth Street.
Broad Street south of Mechanic to Peters Place; Wallace, Linden, Canal, Hudson Av. 50 ft.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 continues the Broad Street corridor south of sheet 2, at 50 feet to an inch with Broad Street running down the page. West of Broad Street the blocks between Peters, Reckless, Le Roy and Waverly Places are residential, with frame dwellings, automobile houses and sheds on lots 20 to 50 feet wide; the 1st Presbyn Church (blue) stands on the north side of the block above Le Roy Place and the Women's Club a little south of it. East of Broad Street a row of frame dwellings fronts the street, and Grace Methodist Church stands on the east side of Broad Street at Harding Road. The blocks east of the avenue lie between Canal Street, Clay Street, Harding Road (printed with Branch Av. in brackets) and Hudson Avenue on the right edge. They hold detached frame houses on deep lots, a private garage of reinforced concrete with a row of auto stalls near Clay Street, and a few sheds. Water pipes of 6, 8 and 10 inches are lettered in the streets, and street widths of 30, 33, 40, 60 and 66 feet are marked. The compass at the upper left points a little west of the page edge, the library stamp crosses the upper centre, and the scale bar at lower right is placed in an unbuilt lot. The sheet number 2 appears above, 4 below, 10 at the left and 6, 30 and 29 at the right, marking the adjoining sheets.
notes: Harding Road is printed with Branch Av. in brackets after it; modern Harding Road becomes Branch Avenue east of Hudson Avenue.
Le Roy Place is the modern Leroy Place.
Harding Road is drawn narrower than its present right-of-way (about 45 against 67 feet), and its junctions with Broad Street and Clay Street fit 2 to 3.5 m from the modern lines.
Broad Street, Peters to Waverly Place; Canal, Clay, Harding Road (Branch Av.), Hudson Av. 50 ft.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 is a residential strip along Broad Street south of Waverly Place, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with Broad Street running down the page. The blocks on the west side, bounded by Waverly Place, Irving Place and Bergen Place, hold frame dwellings with private automobile garages, sheds and a co-op building, on narrow lots opening onto Broad Street and the side streets. House numbers along Broad Street run from about 188 to 280 on the west side and from 205 to 281 on the east side. East of Broad Street one wide block, numbered 6, runs from Broad Street to Hudson Avenue at the right edge. It is divided into deep lots, with frame dwellings facing Broad Street on the west and Hudson Avenue on the east and automobile houses and sheds in the middle, so that much of the block is open back land. A fire alarm box, a hydrant and a telephone pole mark the Broad Street and Bergen Place corner at the bottom. The compass at the left edge is turned a few degrees from the sheet edge. The scale bar and copyright line lie along the bottom edge. Water pipes of 3, 6 and 8 inches are lettered in the streets, and street widths of 60 and 66 feet are marked. The numbers 3 at the top, 27 and 31 at the bottom, 12 at the left and 29 at the right edge name the adjoining sheets.
notes: Bergen Place at the bottom of the sheet is West Bergen Place and East Bergen Place today.
Bergen Place lies along the bottom edge and only its north side is drawn, so its junction with Broad Street was placed from the drawn edge and the street width.
Broad Street, Waverly to Bergen Place; Hudson Av. 50 ft.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows the east side of Red Bank along the north branch of the river, at 50 feet to an inch with north up and slightly to the right. The top third is the river and its shore, with two lettered small boat harbors in the upper left and, beside them, the boat yard of C. P. Irwin, Boat Builder, which stands on the shore with a wooden bulkhead beside it. South of the river lie long narrow lots running down from the shore with a few scattered frame houses, then Union Street and East Front Street, which slope up toward the right across the sheet. The blocks between them and south of East Front Street are built with frame dwellings, a few of brick, and at the lower left near Globe Court a garage, auto repairing and painting shops, a tie shed, S. J. Picot's private property and Reilly's Storage & Transportation Co. The B. P. O. E. building stands in the block between East Front and Mechanic Streets, and the Mechanic St Public School (brick) stands near Mechanic Street east of the middle of the sheet. Washington Street runs down the right-centre of the sheet and a block of small frame houses between Washington and Spring Streets fills the lower right, with the scale bar and library stamp along the bottom edge. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches and fire alarm boxes are lettered in the streets. Sheet numbers 1, 6 and 33 at the edges name the adjoining sheets.
notes: East Front is East Front Street west of Spring Street; Washington is North Washington Street north of East Front Street and Washington Street south of it, in the modern network.
Union Street east of Wharf Avenue is no longer a through street in the modern network.
East end of Union, East Front and Mechanic; Globe Ct, Washington, Spring; boat yards on the river. 50 ft.
placenames: North Branch of Shrewsbury River or Navesink River

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers a residential district of Red Bank east of Broad Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up and slightly to the right. Mechanic Street crosses the top edge, with Wallace Street, Linden Place and Elm Place following at regular intervals down the page and Hudson Avenue forming the left edge below Linden Place. Mount Street, which runs at a slant, bounds the first block at the upper left, where the Independent Co. No. 2 fire department building, with its auto stalls, stands on Mechanic Street near Globe Court. The blocks between these streets are lined with detached frame houses, mostly two storeys with porches, set on narrow lots, with automobile houses and sheds in the rear. A boarding house stands on Wallace Street. Washington Street and Spring Street run down the right side of the sheet through the blocks marked 2, 4, 3 and 5. The block between Linden Place and Elm Place, marked 6, is drawn with long lots that radiate from a slanting line and is only partly built, with a row of houses along Elm Place. At the lower left a compass is drawn beside Hudson Avenue and Canal Street, and the end of the sheet below it is marked 3. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches run in the streets and street widths of 30 and 40 feet are lettered. The scale bar is at the bottom edge. Sheet numbers 5, 2, 3 and 33 at the edges name the adjoining sheets.
notes: Linden Place and Elm Place keep their names; Mount is the modern Mount Street.
Washington is Washington Street south of East Front Street in the modern network.
Mechanic, Wallace, Linden Pl, Elm Pl between Hudson Av and Spring. 50 ft.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows the west end of the Red Bank business district and the river shore, at 50 feet to an inch with north up and slightly to the right. More than half of the sheet is blank paper and river: the north branch of the Shrewsbury or Navesink River crosses the upper part, with a jagged shoreline, a slip and two piers drawn with dashed outlines. Along the lower half run West Front Street and White Street, linked by Maple Avenue at the left. On West Front Street the north side holds frame dwellings, a stuccoed house and a brick residence on deep lots running back to the shore, and a hardware and paint store at the corner of Maple Avenue. The south side has dwellings, then Trinity P. E. Church with its tile parish house. Along White Street stand the J. W. Mount Co. Inc., builders of auto bodies, with auto sales, painting, upholstering and a wood working department, a lumber shed, a patent medicine factory, an awning factory, the Red Bank Steam Laundry and the Liberty Engine Co. No. 2 fire house with its repairing shop. At the left, Riverside Av. runs diagonally between lots drawn at an angle, with second hand furniture and patent medicine shops at the foot of the lots. A fire alarm box stands at the foot of Maple Avenue and White Street. The scale bar is in the lower left; the numbers 14, 18, 1 and 8 at the edges name the adjoining sheets.
notes: West Front is the modern West Front Street; Maple Avenue and White Street keep their names.
The modern junction of Riverside Avenue and West Front Street was not detected on the sheet.
Only Maple Avenue gives control on this sheet: the placement rests on two points on that street.
West Front, White, Maple Av; mostly river. Placed from two Maple Avenue points (helmert). 50 ft.
placenames: North Branch of Shrewsbury River or Navesink River

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 shows the centre of Red Bank west of Broad Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned slightly so that the compass rose at the left points a little east of straight up. Maple Avenue runs down the left side of the sheet, and the cross streets are White Street along the top, Monmouth Street through the middle, then Gold Street and, across the lower part, Oakland Street and Chestnut Street, with Peters Place along the bottom edge. Drummond Place runs south from Monmouth Street to Peters Place on the right. The blocks along White and Monmouth Streets are mixed: frame dwellings in yellow stand beside public garages and automobile sales and repair shops, auto storage buildings with gasoline tanks, a plumber, a tile-roofed shop and, in the right-hand block of Monmouth Street, the Borough Hall with the fire department and the quarters of Relief Engine Co. No. 1, the Y.M.C.A. and a restaurant. South of Gold Street the blocks are mostly dwellings with automobile garages, with a stone-cutting shop, a painting shop, a piano repairer, an upholstery shop and a contractor's storage building. At lower left the First Baptist Church stands on the block between Oakland and Chestnut Streets, with dwellings around it. Water pipes of 4, 6, 8 and 10 inches are lettered in the streets, with hydrants, a fire alarm box at Peters Place and street widths of 30 to 66 feet. Block numbers 2, 3 and 4 are lettered, and the adjoining sheets are 7 to the north, 18 and 9 to the west and southwest, and 10 to the south.
notes: Maple Avenue is lettered 66 feet wide at White Street.
The Borough Hall and fire department stand on the north side of Monmouth Street east of Drummond Place.
White to Peters Place west of Broad. 50 ft.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the industrial western edge of Red Bank, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. West Street runs down the left side and Pearl Street down the middle right, crossed by Oakland Street along the top edge and Chestnut Street through the upper middle of the sheet. North of Chestnut Street the blocks hold rows of frame dwellings with automobile garages along Oakland Street and the Red Bank Armory, a large brick building with a riding hall and a wagon shed, on the left, with the lumber shed and planing mill of Chas. Lewis beside it. South of Chestnut Street the block between West Street and Pearl Street is given over to the Borough Water Works, with its air compressor and receiving basin, a sash and door warehouse, the planing mill and lumber sheds of M. N. Smith and Son, Inc., and, lower down along Pearl Street, the oil tanks, concrete storage buildings, wagon shed and loading platform of the Standard Oil Co. of N.J. The left and bottom of the sheet are crossed by the many tracks of the N.Y. & L.B. R.R., which fan out below into the stalls of a roundhouse and turntable at the bottom edge. East of Pearl Street are more dwellings, some with compass rose and north arrow at the right, and a large area of unbuilt land. Water pipes of 6, 8 and 10 inches are lettered along the streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. Block numbers 2, 3 and 4 are lettered; neighbouring sheets are 18, 8, 10, 11 and 21.
notes: Pearl Street continues south of Chestnut Street along the east side of the oil company property.
The sheet draws the railroad yard and roundhouse of the N.Y. & L.B. R.R. in the lower left; it continues on sheet 11.
Oakland and Chestnut, West and Pearl; rail yard and oil works. 50 ft.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 shows a residential district south of the centre of Red Bank, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned a little so that the compass rose at upper left points slightly east of straight up. Maple Avenue is the main street, running down the sheet from the upper left to the lower middle with its width lettered as 60 and 66 feet. It is crossed by Chestnut Street near the top, Peters Place, Reckless Place, Le Roy Place and Waverly Place at the bottom edge. Drummond Place enters from the top just east of Peters Place. West of Maple Avenue a single long block holds a row of frame dwellings and automobile garages set back on deep lots, with a few dwellings finished in tile. East of Maple Avenue the blocks between Peters, Reckless, Le Roy and Waverly Places are likewise mostly detached frame dwellings, many with a garage at the rear. Shrewsbury Academy stands in the lowest block on Le Roy Place, a heated school building with its own lighting, and a foundation for an addition is drawn beside it. The upper right and the lower left are mostly blank paper belonging to the adjoining sheets. Water pipes of 3, 4, 6 and 10 inches run in the streets, with hydrants. Block numbers 1, 3, 4 and 5 are lettered; the neighbouring sheets are 8 to the north, 9 and 12 around the edges, and 3 on the right.
notes: Le Roy Place is Leroy Place in the modern street data.
Peters, Reckless, Le Roy and Waverly are all printed with 'Pl.', written out here as Place.
Maple Av, Peters to Waverly Place. 50 ft.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers the railroad corridor on the south side of Red Bank, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The upper two thirds of the sheet is largely open ground crossed by the tracks of the N.Y. & L.B. R.R., which fan out at the upper left into a roundhouse with its turntable and radiating engine stalls, and run to the lower right in a bundle of main tracks with a long freight depot and platforms at upper centre. A curved track loops round to a store house at the left, and the tracks of a second line run down the left edge. The built-up part lies along the bottom of the sheet, in blocks between Central Avenue on the left, Berry Street, South Pearl Street and Beach Street at the bottom edge. These blocks hold small frame dwellings in rows with a few automobile garages and a sash and door warehouse near the left edge. At the lower right the Monmouth Mutual Supply Co. ice house, cold storage and freezing tanks stand beside the tracks, with an ice house and a coal pile. Pearl Street enters from the top near the upper right and the right edge shows dwellings and small buildings on narrow lots facing it. Streets are lettered 50 and 60 feet wide, and water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are drawn along Beach Street. Block numbers 1 to 6 are lettered. Neighbouring sheets are 9, 12, 22, 26 and 27.
notes: Beach is the modern West Bergen Place.
Most of the sheet is railroad land, with no streets.
Railroad yard; West, Oakland, Chestnut, Herbert, Leonard; Beach (West Bergen Pl). 50 ft.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 lies at the south end of the main part of Red Bank, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and slightly turned, with the compass rose at the left. Maple Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet from top to bottom, with Waverly Place and Irving Place crossing it on the right and Beach and Bergen Place along the bottom edge. Arthur Place is drawn to the right, marked as not open. West of Maple Avenue is a long block of detached frame dwellings with automobile garages on deep lots, with the tracks of the N.Y. & L.B. R.R. coming in from the lower left. At the lower end of that block stand the plant of the Fred D. Wikoff Co., dealers in hay, feed and coal, with a feed mill, grain bins, a corn cracker and sheller, an attrition mill, a wagon shed and a coal dump, and beyond it in the lower left a large pink building along the railroad. East of Maple Avenue the blocks between Waverly Place, Irving Place and Bergen Place hold dwellings with automobile garages, some at the rear of lots with house numbers 179 to 237 on Maple Avenue. Water pipes of 3 and 6 inches run in the streets, with hydrants, a fire alarm box at Irving Place and street widths lettered 36, 50, 60 and 66 feet. Block numbers 1 to 4 are lettered and the neighbouring sheets are 10 to the north, 11 and 27 below, and 4 on the right.
notes: Arthur Place is lettered as not open.
Beach and Bergen Place together are the modern West Bergen Place and East Bergen Place, which meet at Maple Avenue.
The coal and feed buildings of the Fred D. Wikoff Co. are drawn along the track beside Maple Avenue.
Maple Av, Waverly to Bergen Place; Arthur Pl. Three points (exact fit). 50 ft.

sheet-13-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 13 shows the northern tip of Red Bank on the North Branch of the Shrewsbury River, or Navesink River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up. Bridge Avenue, 66 feet wide, runs north along the west side to the old road bridge over the river, and Railroad Avenue runs north along the east side beside the tracks of the railroad, which cross the river on their own bridge. Prospect Street crosses the bottom of the part between the two avenues; the blocks south of it are on sheet 15. The large block between Bridge and Railroad Avenues is occupied by the works of The C. E. Conover Co., manufacturers of waterproof cloth and dry goods novelties: brick storage, packing and shipping, and sewing buildings, with treating tanks, a septic plant and a gate house near the river. A row of frame dwellings faces Prospect Street, and smaller dwellings, junk sheds and stables stand along Bridge Avenue. East of Railroad Avenue are a few large dwellings and a club house in block 2, with the river shore curving round the north-east corner. West of Bridge Avenue, block 3 lies along the shore with a boat house. Water pipes run in Bridge Avenue, Railroad Avenue and Prospect Street, with a fire alarm box at Railroad Avenue. The upper left corner of the sheet holds a separate inset (part 2) of the Tintern Manor Water Co. works.
notes: The area has been rebuilt around the NJ 35 bridge approach; Railroad Avenue is today Morford Place and Bridge Avenue is North Bridge Avenue.
Placed from three block corners at Prospect carried from sheet 15, which repeats the block; low to medium confidence, especially at the north end by the river.

Red Bank, 50 ft to an inch. Main map: north end of Bridge Av, Railroad Av, Prospect, C.E. Conover Co. works, Navesink River (area rebuilt around NJ 35). Inset top left: Tintern Manor Water Co. on Newman Springs Rd at Swimming River, with a break in the road (470 ft dimension). Lead configures.
placenames: North Branch of Shrewsbury River or Navesink River

sheet-13-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 13 is an inset in the upper left corner of the sheet showing the works of the Tintern Manor Water Co. on the south side of Newman Springs Road, west of Red Bank where the road crosses the Swimming River. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up. The road is drawn with a break: a dimension line gives the distance from the works to the river bank as 470 feet, much more than is drawn, and the bridge over the Swimming River beyond the break is left out of this part. The plant is a group of brick buildings: a filter house with twelve wooden filter tanks 18 feet deep, an engine room with engines of 450 and 250 horsepower, a boiler house with five boilers of 150 horsepower, a centrifugal pump room, a concrete coal shed and a brick chimney 50 feet high. A long note lists the equipment: two Worthington compound duplex pumps of 6,000,000 gallons a day, another of 2,000,000 gallons, three Lawrence centrifugal pumps and a 7 1/2 kilowatt generator, with electric light, steam heat and hose on a wheel cart. A 36 inch water pipe runs from the works north to Newman Springs Road, 33 feet wide, and east along it toward Red Bank. A hydrant stands beside the coal shed.
notes: Anchored on one hand-picked point on Newman Springs Road, 470 ft west of the Swimming River's west bank along the modern road, with the scale and rotation of the Red Bank sheets assumed; low confidence (10 m or more).
The bridge piece east of the break in the road is not part of the mask.

Red Bank, 50 ft to an inch. Main map: north end of Bridge Av, Railroad Av, Prospect, C.E. Conover Co. works, Navesink River (area rebuilt around NJ 35). Inset top left: Tintern Manor Water Co. on Newman Springs Rd at Swimming River, with a break in the road (470 ft dimension). Lead configures.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 shows the west edge of Red Bank on the north side of the North Branch of the Shrewsbury River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Railroad Avenue runs down the left side, with Allen Place crossing it above the middle and West Front Street along the bottom, and Riverside Avenue sweeps from the upper left to the lower right in a long curve toward the lower right corner. A narrow triangular block of dwellings lies between Railroad Avenue and Riverside Avenue, and below it between Allen Place and West Front Street are further frame dwellings, auto sheds, a tenement and small shops. Riverside Avenue is lined with dwellings on its lower side and on its upper, river side by larger detached houses with garages on deep lots running down to the river, whose shore is a heavy line with the water tinted blue-green and the note North Branch of Shrewsbury River or Navesink River along it. At the lower right, where Riverside Avenue meets West Front Street, a brick-filled undertaker's building and a store stand on the wedge-shaped corner. West Street and Pearl Street run out of West Front Street at the bottom of the sheet. Pipes of 4 and 6 inches, with hydrants and a fire alarm box, are lettered, and street widths of 40 to 64 feet. Block numbers 1 to 3 are lettered; the neighbouring sheets are 13 above, 15 at the left, 17 and 18 below, and 7 on the right.
notes: Railroad Avenue is the modern Morford Place.
West Street and Pearl Street are lettered at the bottom edge in small type: medium confidence.
The river shore is drawn as a heavy line along the top and right.
Riverside Av, Allen Pl, West Front; railroad. Riverside Av / West Front realigned, not used. 50 ft.
placenames: North Branch of Shrewsbury River or Navesink River

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers the west end of Red Bank's riverfront and the railroad station area, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. West Front Street runs along the bottom of the sheet. Bridge Avenue rises from it through the middle and Railroad Avenue runs up the right side beside the tracks of the C. R. R. of N. J., with the freight depot and platforms. Rector Place curves from the bottom left to the upper middle, with Shrewsbury Avenue at the bottom left and a steel bridge of the N.Y. & L.B. R.R. crossing the lower left corner. Between Rector Place and the river at the upper left is a long block of large frame dwellings with boat houses on deep lots running to the North Branch of Shrewsbury River or Navesink River, and at the head of the block the Jersey Central Traction Co. sub-station. Between Rector Place and Bridge Avenue are more dwellings and a bottling works. On the right of Bridge Avenue Prospect, Willow (not opened) and Depot Streets cut the blocks, which hold dwellings, the Austic Furniture Factory, the Monmouth Ice Co. with its freezing tanks and ice house, a contractor's yard, the Quartermaster Corps U.S.A. warehouse and the large Sigmund Eisner Co. warehouse on the corner of West Front Street. Riverside Avenue and Allen Place appear at the right edge. Block numbers 1 to 4 are lettered; neighbouring sheets are 13, 14, 16 and 17.
notes: Railroad Avenue is the modern Morford Place.
Bridge Avenue north of West Front Street is now North Bridge Avenue.
Willow is lettered not opened; the modern street at that spot is Brower Street.
Bridge Av, Rector Pl, West Front, Willow; Prospect at top. 50 ft.
placenames: North Branch of Shrewsbury River or Navesink River

sheet-16-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 16 is the main map of the sheet, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up, and covers the western edge of Red Bank along the North Branch of the Shrewsbury River, also called the Navesink River. Shrewsbury Avenue runs down the east edge of the part; Monmouth Street leaves it eastward at the upper right and De Forest Avenue and Oakland Street meet it near the bottom. The river fills the middle of the sheet, bending from the upper right towards the lower left, and most of the ground west of it is left blank, with a few scattered dwellings and outbuildings in the lower left corner beyond the river. Along Shrewsbury Avenue the frontage is lightly built: a row of dwellings with outbuildings on large deep lots, numbered house by house, and, at the top right, a coal, grain and wood yard with long storage sheds beside a railroad that crosses the avenue on a diagonal. Lot lines run back from the avenue to the water. The block number 1 is lettered in the lower right block. A large north arrow and compass stand in the left margin. The part leaves out the inset in the upper left corner, which is georeferenced separately as part 2, and adjoins sheet 17 on the east and sheet 20 below.
notes: Shrewsbury Avenue is also lettered with a width of 68 feet at the Monmouth Street and Oakland Street crossings.
De Forest Avenue (west of Shrewsbury Avenue) is today Deforrest Avenue.
Oakland Street east of Shrewsbury Avenue meets De Forest Avenue across the avenue; the modern nodes are about 7 m apart.
Two parts: main (Shrewsbury Av at the right edge, De Forest Av, river; 50 ft) and inset top left (West Front at Shrewsbury Av and the concrete bridge; scale taken as 100 ft). Both weak.
placenames: North Branch of the Shrewsbury River or Navesink River

sheet-16-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 16 is the boxed inset in the upper left corner, bounded by a heavy double line and with its own north arrow pointing up. It shows a short stretch of West Front Street and the upper end of Shrewsbury Avenue, drawn at a smaller scale than the main map (the street widths fit about 100 feet to an inch, which has not been confirmed from a printed scale). West Front Street crosses the inset from the upper left, where it runs over a concrete bridge across the North Branch of the Shrewsbury River, towards the junction with Shrewsbury Avenue at the right edge; north of the junction the avenue is lettered Rector Place. A pair of railroad tracks marked as the N.Y. & L.B. R.R. cross the inset from the upper centre to the lower right. Buildings are few: a shed beside the street at the right, a dwelling and an automobile garage near the bridge, and a long narrow storage building in the lower middle. The river curves through the lower half. Block numbers 1, 15 and 16 appear in the inset. The inset repeats ground that is drawn in full on neighbouring sheets and is georeferenced from a single junction, so its placement is approximate.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked junction (Shrewsbury Avenue meeting West Front Street, taken as modern Rector Place and West Front Street) with the scale and rotation assumed, so confidence is low.
Modern Rector Place is the short link between Shrewsbury Avenue and West Front Street; the sheet letters Rector Place on the far side of West Front Street.
Two parts: main (Shrewsbury Av at the right edge, De Forest Av, river; 50 ft) and inset top left (West Front at Shrewsbury Av and the concrete bridge; scale taken as 100 ft). Both weak.
placenames: North Branch of the Shrewsbury River or Navesink River

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 is a central manufacturing and business district of Red Bank at 50 feet to an inch, with north up. It lies between West Front Street along the top and Monmouth Street and Oakland Street below, and is cut from upper left to lower right by the double tracks of the railroad, with a second line and sidings crossing the sheet east of Bridge Avenue. Shrewsbury Avenue runs down the left edge, Bridge Avenue across the middle and West Street along the right edge. The largest works are the Sigmund Eisner Co. clothing and uniform factory at the upper left, a group of large brick and frame buildings; a second Eisner building with a storage warehouse stands south of Bridge Avenue. Between Bridge Avenue and the railroad the blocks hold lumber yards and sheds (John T. Burrowes Co., Inc.), a coal and wood yard and other trades; a public service garage stands near Monmouth Street, and an ice company lies south of the street. Dwellings with outbuildings fill the narrow blocks along West Street on the right. Water pipes and hydrants are marked in every street, and street widths of 50 and 60 feet are lettered at several crossings. Blocks are numbered 1 to 5.
notes: Shrewsbury Avenue junctions were measured with the street set to a 60 ft width; without that setting the detector paired the wrong lines at the sheet edge.
Neither a hand pick nor a carried point was needed; the part is placed from 7 detected junctions.
Shrewsbury Av, West Front to Oakland; Sigmund Eisner Co. 50 ft.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 shows the heart of old Red Bank's business district at 50 feet to an inch, with north up. West Front Street crosses the top diagonally and Monmouth Street and Oakland Street run across the middle and bottom; West Street forms the left edge, Pearl Street the middle and Maple Avenue the right edge. Wall Street and Water Street cut through the large blocks north of Monmouth Street, and Riverside Avenue leaves West Front Street at the top towards the river, with White Street lettered at the right edge. The blocks along West Front, Wall and Water Streets are densely built with brick stores, a garage, a hall for the Knights of Columbus and another hall, a Baptist church, offices and many small dwellings, drawn in pink, blue and yellow. South of Monmouth Street the blocks are residential, with rows of dwellings, a public school on Oakland Street and a few shops at the corners. Buildings along Monmouth Street are numbered, and the rear lot lines show the ragged outlines of an older town. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches and hydrants are shown in the streets. A compass at the top points north. The sheet adjoins sheet 17 on the west, sheet 14 above and sheets 8 and 9 below.
notes: West Street is detected inconsistently at the left sheet edge; its junction with Monmouth Street was placed by hand at the crossing of the street's water pipes.
Only three junctions were detected and one placed by hand, so confidence is low to medium.
Monmouth, Wall, Water, Pearl, Maple; West Street junctions excluded. 50 ft.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers the marshes and meadows west of Red Bank at 50 feet to an inch, with north up, and is almost entirely unbuilt. A winding arm of Swimming River crosses the upper left and meets a second branch near the middle left, and the ground between and below the streams is lettered Marsh Land. At the right, a short stretch of platted streets is drawn: Locust Avenue runs across the upper right with Edgar and Slocum Streets crossing it, and long narrow lots reach down towards the marsh. Only one dwelling and a small outbuilding appear on the whole sheet, near Locust Avenue at the right edge; several lot lines at the lower right run out into the marsh without buildings. A long diagonal line crosses the marsh from the lower left, and a dash-dot match line, with the corner letters A and B, runs along the bottom. The sheet carries a compass and north arrow at the upper left, and block numbers 1 to 4. It overlaps the left edge of sheet 20, which repeats the same blocks at Locust Avenue.
notes: Placed from one block corner read on sheet 20 (anchored, scale and rotation taken from sheet 20), so confidence is low.
The lettering Arbitrary runs along the street at the right edge, beside Slocum; it appears to mark a street line, not a name.
Swimming River marsh west of Locust Av; anchored on one point carried from sheet 20. 50 ft.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 shows a residential district west of Red Bank at 50 feet to an inch, with north up. Leighton Avenue runs down the left-centre of the sheet and Shrewsbury Avenue down the right edge; across them run De Forest Avenue near the top, Locust Avenue, Herbert Street, Earle Street and Leonard Street at the bottom. Slocum Street lies along the left edge, where the blocks west of Leighton Avenue are cut into long narrow lots running down to the swampy ground at the far left. Almost every building is a frame dwelling with its outbuildings; a few garages and sheds stand behind the houses. The blocks between Leighton and Shrewsbury Avenues are numbered 2, 3 and 5 and the block above Locust Avenue 1. A church of the First Reformed congregation stands on a corner of the block at lower right, and a few stores and a brick building face Shrewsbury Avenue on the right edge. A blue building with a cross-shaped plan stands at the upper left. Water pipes are marked in the streets, and street widths of 50 and 60 feet are lettered at several corners. A compass stands at the upper left. The sheet overlaps sheet 19 at the left and sheet 16 above.
notes: Shrewsbury Avenue junctions are measured with the street set to a 60 ft width; at the narrower default the detector paired a block line and the scale came out 4 percent small.
Earle Street is today Earl Street.
De Forest Avenue is today Deforrest Avenue.
Leonard Street at Shrewsbury Avenue is today West Leonard Street.
Shrewsbury Av, Locust, Leighton, Herbert, Earle, De Forest Av. 50 ft.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 covers the west side of Red Bank between Oakland Street at the top and Leonard Street near the bottom, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up. Shrewsbury Avenue runs down the left edge, Bridge Avenue down the middle and West Street along the right edge, with the double tracks and sidings of the Central Railroad of New Jersey cutting diagonally through the right-hand blocks. Chestnut Street and Herbert Street cross the sheet between Oakland and Leonard Streets. The sheet is mostly dwellings with outbuildings on the left and centre, with a Roman Catholic church (St. Anthony) on Chestnut Street, the Shrewsbury Avenue public school, and a fire department building with a hose company on the left edge. In the upper right the works of the Roberts Safety Water Tube Boiler Co. fill a large block beside the railroad, with machine shops, an erecting shop and an assembling department, and a lumber yard with long sheds stands at the extreme right. Contractors' yards and a warehouse lie in the block below Herbert Street, and an electric company building and warehouses stand beside the tracks. Street widths and water mains are lettered throughout. Blocks are numbered 1 to 8, and a compass sits at the right.
notes: The railroad is lettered C.R.R. of N.J.; its modern line was used as extra control at Chestnut Street.
Leonard Street between Shrewsbury and Bridge Avenues is today East Leonard Street.
Fitted at 1.9 m RMSE, which is higher than neighbouring sheets; the Shrewsbury Avenue and West Street junctions carry the largest residuals.
Shrewsbury Av to the railroad, Oakland to Leonard; Bridge Av. 50 ft.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 covers the western edge of Red Bank at 50 feet to an inch, with north up, between Catherine Street at the upper edge and Beech Street along the bottom. Shrewsbury Avenue runs down the left edge and Bridge Avenue down the middle; River Street and Cedar Street run across the sheet between them, and the broad railroad lines of the Central Railroad of New Jersey fill the right edge. The blocks are only partly built: dwellings with outbuildings stand along Bridge Avenue and the main streets, and the large blocks between River Street and Beech Street hold a few scattered buildings on deep lots. Public buildings include the River Street school (No. 7) at the left centre, the Beech Street school (No. 5) near the bottom, and the Calvary Baptist Church on River Street. A small works and a few stores lie along Shrewsbury Avenue, and a contractor's yard and sheds stand by the railroad at the upper right. Street widths of 50 and 60 feet are lettered, with water pipes and hydrants in the streets. Blocks are numbered 1 to 8. A compass is drawn at the right.
notes: The railroad is lettered C.R.R. of N.J.
Beech Street is today West Bergen Place; the same street is lettered Beach on sheet 23.
Shrewsbury Avenue junctions at Catherine Street and Beech Street were not detected; the part rests on Bridge Avenue and River Street.
Shrewsbury Av to Bridge Av, Leonard to Beech (West Bergen Pl). 50 ft.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 shows the south-western edge of Red Bank at 50 feet to an inch, with north up, around Pintard Avenue (Tilton Avenue) near the middle. Catherine Street crosses the upper part, River Street the middle, Bank Street below it and Beach Street along the bottom edge. The left half of the sheet is open land: swamp land at the top left, a few scattered dwellings, a factory making men's clothing in the middle left, and Swimming River curving in from the left edge to the bottom. East of Pintard Avenue the blocks are built up with dwellings and outbuildings along Catherine Street, River Street and Bank Street, with a church on the street north of Catherine Street, a small group of public buildings coloured pink and blue near Bank Street, and a few stores. Numbered blocks 1 to 6 appear, with house numbers along the frontages. A dash-dot match line with the letters H and A runs along the top, and a compass sits at the upper left. The sheet adjoins sheet 24 on the east, sheet 19 above and sheet 25 below.
notes: Pintard Avenue (Tilton Avenue) is today Tilton Avenue.
Beach is today West Bergen Place.
All control points lie along Pintard Avenue, so the part is a helmert fit and its rotation and scale are from neighbouring sheets; confidence is low.
Tilton Av (Pintard Av), Catherine to Beach; marsh. Points along Tilton Av only (helmert). 50 ft.

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 covers a residential district on the west side of Red Bank, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up. It shows four blocks between Leighton Avenue on the west and Shrewsbury Avenue along the east edge, from Leonard Street at the top of the sheet through Catherine, River and Bank Streets down to Beach Street at the bottom edge, together with the east ends of the blocks west of Leighton Avenue (block 4 at upper left, blocks 1, 3 and 6 below it). Block numbers 2, 5, 7 and 8 lie between Leighton and Shrewsbury Avenues. Almost every lot holds a frame dwelling with its outbuildings, mostly two storeys with porches, together with private automobile garages, sheds and chicken coops. Business is confined to the Shrewsbury Avenue frontage on the east: a hardware and paint store, brick stores with tile roofs and a frame building marked F at the corner of Catherine Street, and a few stores in the block between River and Bank Streets. A small winery stands behind the houses on the south side of Catherine Street, and a two-storey lodging house on Leighton Avenue near River Street. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches run in every street, with hydrants and a fire alarm box at the Leighton Avenue corners. At the upper left the edge of a ravine is drawn with the note 'Top of bank'. The street widths are lettered: 60 feet for Leighton and Shrewsbury Avenues, 55 feet for Catherine Street and 50 feet for Leonard Street. House numbers run along every frontage. The adjoining sheets are 20 to the north, 22 to the east, 23 to the west and 25 to the south.
notes: Beach is the modern West Bergen Place.
Leonard is West Leonard Street at Leighton Avenue; at Shrewsbury Avenue it meets both East and West Leonard Street, which are offset.
Shrewsbury Avenue lies along the east edge of the sheet, and only its west side is drawn.
Red Bank, 50 ft to an inch. Leighton Av to Shrewsbury Av, Leonard to Beach (West Bergen Pl). Pilot sheet.

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 covers the southwest part of Red Bank, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north up. The built-up part lies between Beach at the top edge and Newman Springs Road, which crosses the lower third of the sheet, and between Leighton Avenue and Shrewsbury Avenue, with the blocks west of Leighton Avenue reaching toward the Swimming River at the left. Sunset Avenue and West Side Avenue cross the sheet east to west. Blocks 1 to 5 above West Side Avenue hold mostly frame dwellings with outbuildings; blocks 6 to 10 below it, between Carmen Place, Clifford Place, Leighton Avenue and Clinton Avenue, are less filled, and carry the Sweet Clover Farms Dairy and, at the corner of Shrewsbury Avenue and Newman Springs Road, the Mecca Inn. A fire department hose company building stands in block 9 and a fire alarm box at Shrewsbury Avenue and Sunset Avenue. Below Newman Springs Road, which also marks the Borough limits, the sheet shows large unbuilt tracts (blocks 11, 12 and 13, and lots 1 to 4) with a few farm buildings. At the left the Swimming River runs down the sheet with a Borough garbage dump on its east bank, and a small stream crosses block 6. Water pipes of 6 inches run in the streets, and a 30 inch pipe of the Tintern Manor Water Co. runs along Newman Springs Road. Street widths are lettered, 50 to 66 feet. The adjoining sheets are 23 and 24 to the north, 26 to the east, and the lower margin has the printed scale bar of 100 feet to one inch.
notes: Beach is the modern West Bergen Place.

Pintard Avenue (Tilton Avenue) is today's Tilton Avenue; West Side Avenue and Sunset Avenue are today's West Westside Avenue and West Sunset Avenue; Carmen Place, Clifford Place and Clinton Avenue are today's Carmen Place, Clifford Place and Clinton Place.
The sheet says 100 feet to an inch although the other low-numbered sheets are 50 feet; the fit gives about 3.94 px/ft. atlas.json should carry scale_ft 100 for this sheet.

St. Marys Place, Westside Avenue, Sunset Avenue and Drummond Avenue are lettered only at the right edge, in the margin shared with sheet 26. Westside Avenue and Clinton Avenue were read at modest resolution.
Tilton Av to Shrewsbury Av, Beach to Newman Springs Rd; Sunset, West Side Av. 100 ft (printed).

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 covers the south side of Red Bank between Shrewsbury Avenue at the left and South Pearl Avenue at the right, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north up. Beach runs along the top edge and Newman Springs Road, also the Borough limits, crosses the lower part. Between them lie blocks of frame dwellings along Shrewsbury Avenue, Sunset Avenue, Westside Avenue and Drummond Avenue, with a church and a hall at the top left near Shrewsbury Avenue, and St. Marys Place cutting through block 1. Sunset Avenue and Westside Avenue jog where they cross Bridge Avenue and Shrewsbury Avenue. The New York and Long Branch Railroad runs north to south through the middle of the sheet. East of it a lumber yard of L. J. Sieling, Engineering Contractor, has an area of piled lumber 5 to 18 feet high, and below it stand the plant of the Public Service Electric Co. (heat, steam, light, electric), with a Reservoir to its east. Central Avenue and South Pearl Avenue run down the east side with block 4 between them, and a short yellow strip at the lower right is a building of an adjoining sheet. Below Newman Springs Road the sheet shows large unbuilt numbered tracts (blocks 11, 12 and 13, lots 42 to 53) with a few farm buildings. A 30 inch water pipe of the Tintern Manor Water Co. runs along Newman Springs Road. The adjoining sheets are 22 and 25 to the west and north, 27 to the east and 57 to the south.
notes: Beach is the modern West Bergen Place.
Willow is today's Willow Street; Sunset Avenue is West Sunset Avenue, Sunset Avenue and Sunset Avenue East in OpenStreetMap, and Westside Avenue is West Westside Avenue west of Bridge Avenue.
The sheet says 100 feet to an inch; the fit gives about 3.97 px/ft. atlas.json should carry scale_ft 100 for this sheet.
Street names were read from the overview-sized sheet rather than from full-resolution crops of every label.
Shrewsbury Av to S. Pearl, railroad, lumber yard, Public Service Electric, reservoir. 100 ft (printed).

sheet-27.description: Sheet 27 covers the south-east edge of Red Bank, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north up. Bergen Place runs along the top edge, South Pearl Avenue forms the left edge of the built-up area, and Broad Street runs down the right side. Newman Springs Road, which carries the Borough limits, crosses the sheet diagonally below the middle and Thomas Avenue and White Road close it at the bottom right. The double-track New York and Long Branch Railroad enters at the top near Maple Street and sweeps south-east through blocks 2 and 4 to cross Broad Street and Newman Springs Road at the right edge. Housing is confined to the frontages along Bergen Place and Broad Street and to the east side of South Pearl Avenue, where the Bruno Bros. soda water bottling works stands among dwellings; the rest of the sheet is open land divided into large numbered tracts (blocks 1 to 6, 13, and lots 20 to 39 along Thomas Avenue), with a row of narrow platted lots. A reservoir outline is cut by the left edge and continues on sheet 26. Below Newman Springs Road the Orioles Base Ball Park has a curved grandstand drawn in yellow. A 36 inch water pipe of the Tintern Manor Water Co. follows Newman Springs Road. The adjoining sheets are 26 to the west, 31 to the north-east, 32 and 58 to the south and 57 to the south-west.
notes: Bergen Place is the modern West Bergen Place west of Maple and East Bergen Place east of it; Pinkney Road is today's Pinckney Road.

Fit rests on Broad Street points and four points carried from sheet 26 (South Pearl Avenue corners and the reservoir). Pinckney Road at Broad Street was rejected at 6.9 m; the modern junction does not agree with the drawn one.
Broad / S. Pearl, railroad, Newman Springs Rd, ball park; points carried from sheet 26. 100 ft (printed).

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 covers the south-east side of Red Bank where Branch Avenue runs south-east from Tower Hill Avenue to the Borough limits, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north up. Branch Avenue and Spring run down the sheet as two converging diagonals, enclosing a long wedge of narrow lots (block 2) built up with frame dwellings, with the Monmouth Dairy Co. and a fire alarm box at the Bergen Place corner. On the west side South street runs down the left edge, with Brown Place and Bergen Place leaving it at an angle toward Branch Avenue, and Madison Avenue and Pinkney Road crossing it lower down. The lots between Brown Place and Bergen Place are small and mostly built, those further south are larger and sparsely built, and a street labelled Not Named, Not Opened runs between blocks 4 and 5. At the lower right a dash-dot line marks the Red Bank Borough limits, and beyond it open ground. Street widths of 40, 50 and 60 feet are lettered, water pipes of 6 and 10 inches follow Tower Hill Avenue and Branch Avenue, and a yellow strip along Spring is part of a building drawn on the adjoining sheet. The adjoining sheets are 29 and 30 to the north, 31 and 32 to the west and south, and 45 and 71 to the east and south-east.
notes: Bergen Place is the modern East Bergen Place here; Pinkney Road is today's Pinckney Road; South is today's South Street.
A street lettered Not Named, Not Opened lies between blocks 4 and 5.
Spring / Tower Hill Avenue falls at the top edge of the sheet and was fitted from the drawn edges.
Branch / Spring wedge, South, Brown, Bergen, Madison, Pinkney. 100 ft (printed).

sheet-29.description: Sheet 29 shows a residential and small commercial district on the south-west side of Red Bank, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up. The sheet is divided by three streets: Hudson Avenue along the left edge, South street running down the middle, and Branch Avenue crossing the upper right as a long diagonal toward the lower right. Brown Place closes the lower right corner and Tower Hill Avenue enters from the right edge near the compass. Block 1, between Hudson Avenue and South, is filled with frame dwellings on deep lots with outbuildings, garages and a few tile or brick buildings drawn in red; the Hudson House, a building lettered 'Hudson House, heat, steam, lights, elec.', stands on the Hudson Avenue frontage. Block 2 lies between South, Branch Avenue and Brown Place and has dwellings along its edges with large open lots behind them; the lots along the Branch Avenue side are drawn with irregular wedge shapes. Water pipes of 6 and 10 inches run in Branch Avenue and Tower Hill Avenue and a 6 inch pipe runs down South street. Street widths of 50 to 66 feet are lettered. The sheet carries the usual scale of feet and a compass rose. The adjoining sheets are 28 to the east, 30 to the north-east, 3 and 4 to the west and 31 below.
notes: Hudson Avenue, South, Branch Avenue, Brown Place and Tower Hill Avenue keep their names today (South is South Street).
Placed from four street junctions only (RMSE 1.3 m, no leave-one-out); medium confidence.
Hudson, South, Branch, Brown. 50 ft.

sheet-30.description: Sheet 30 shows the Red Bank school district between Hudson Avenue and Spring, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned: north points toward the upper right at roughly 30 degrees, so Harding Road runs diagonally from upper left to lower right across the middle. Elm Place runs parallel to it along the top, with Horace between block 1 and block 2 joining the two. Branch Avenue enters from the left edge and runs down the left side to meet Tower Hill Avenue along the bottom, with Spring running down the right edge. The centre is taken up by the school grounds: the Junior High School, a large brick building drawn in pink with its auditorium at the right and fire escapes lettered, and the Senior High School, a fireproof building marked as built in 1918 and drawn in brown. Frame dwellings stand in regular rows on the north side of Elm Place and Harding Road and on both sides of Horace; two rows of houses on Elm Place and Harding Road are numbered 1 to 29 and 31 to 49. Block 3 below the schools has larger lots with dwellings, garages and a kennel, and a fire alarm station sits at the junction of Spring and Harding Road. Water pipes of 6 and 10 inches run in Branch Avenue and Tower Hill Avenue, and street widths of 40 to 53 feet are lettered. Adjoining sheets are 3 and 29 to the west, 6 above, 33 to the right and 28 and 45 below.
notes: Harding Road is lettered with the alternative name Park Place.
The sheet is drawn turned about 33 degrees from north-up; the fit gives about 7.8 px/ft.

Branch Avenue / Tower Hill Avenue was hand-picked: the detector put it 430 px north of the Tower Hill row, which is drawn from its north edge only (sheet edge at the south). The point sits half the lettered 50 ft width below the north edge.
Elm Place / Hudson Avenue lies just above the top edge of the sheet and was fitted from the drawn street edges.
High school grounds; Elm, Horace, Harding (Park Pl.), Tower Hill. Sheet turned about 33 deg. 50 ft.

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 covers a thinly built area on the south-west side of Red Bank, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up. Bergen Place crosses the sheet from left to right at about its centre, Broad runs down the left edge and South down the right edge, and Pinkney Road forms the bottom edge. Hudson Avenue enters from the top and ends at Bergen Place. Madison Avenue joins South from the east near the lower right. The upper half is mostly open land: block 4 at the upper left is blank, and block 1 at the upper right has dwellings and garages along its edges (the Hudson Avenue and South frontages). Below Bergen Place, block 2 fills the rest of the sheet with a few frame dwellings along the Bergen Place and Broad frontages, a pink tile building near the middle left, and the Red Bank Nursery, with its greenhouse, corn crib and other outbuildings, in the lower left. Large tracts of unbuilt land lie between, bounded by irregular lot lines. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches run in Broad, Hudson Avenue, South and Bergen Place; street widths of 60 and 66 feet are lettered. A fire alarm box and hydrant stand at Broad and Bergen Place. The adjoining sheets are 27 to the west, 29 to the north, 28 to the east and 32 below.
notes: Bergen Place is the modern East Bergen Place; Pinkney Road is today's Pinckney Road; Broad and South are Broad Street and South Street.
Madison Avenue / South Street and Pinckney Road / South Street were hand-picked from the drawn street edges (Pinkney is drawn from its north edge only at the sheet bottom).
Broad, Hudson, South around Bergen Pl; Red Bank Nursery. 50 ft.

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 covers the open south-western outskirts of Red Bank, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north up. Pinkney Road runs across the top, Broad along the left edge, South runs down from Pinkney Road toward the centre of the sheet, and White Road crosses the lower third. The New York and Long Branch Railroad enters at the left edge and runs south-east across the sheet, crossing White Road near the centre; the North Monroe Avenue and Monroe Avenue streets lie to its west and the lots along them are numbered. The Red Bank Borough limits are drawn as a dash-dot line curving across the upper half, and a 36 inch water pipe of the Tintern Manor Water Co. crosses at about one third of the way down. Most of the sheet is open land, blocks 1, 2 and 6 being undivided tracts with only a few farm buildings; small numbered lots, many with a dwelling, lie in blocks 3, 4 and 5 west of the railroad along Broad, North Monroe Avenue and Monroe Avenue. Industrial uses are a Texas Co. oil depot with tanks and an office near South, a coal chute and trestle beside the railroad, and the Consolidated Gas Co. plant with a gasometer of 300,000 cubic feet capacity at the southern edge of block 5. Several long yellow sheds stand at the far right. Street widths of 30, 45 and 66 feet are lettered. The adjoining sheets are 31 and 28 to the north, 27 to the west, 58 below and 71 to the east.
notes: Pinkney Road is today's Pinckney Road; Broad and South are Broad Street and South Street here; North Monroe Avenue keeps its name, and Monroe Avenue and White Road keep theirs.
The modern Monroe Avenue / North Monroe Avenue node sits about 5 m from the drawn junction and was left out of the fit.

Broad Street / Pinckney Road, Broad Street / White Road, Broad Street / Monroe Avenue and South Street / Pinckney Road lie at the left edge or on narrow streets and rest partly on the drawn street edges.
Broad, South, White Rd, Monroe, railroad, Texas Co., Consolidated Gas Co. 100 ft.

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers the area immediately north and east of the centre of Red Bank, lying on a turned sheet whose north arrow points up and to the right. The map is bounded at the top by the North Branch of the Shrewsbury River, here also called the Navesink River, which runs across the upper part of the sheet with a brook entering it from a steep, walled ravine. Beneath the river lies a large unsubdivided estate, block 1, holding a group of lettered frame dwellings with garages. East Front Street crosses the middle of the sheet from the bridge over the brook at the upper left to the right edge, and the built-up blocks 4, 5 and 9 lie along it and along Prospect Avenue, with small frame dwellings, many with automobile garages, a cleaning and dyeing shop and a news stand. Mechanic and Mc Laren Streets cross the sheet from left to right, while Throckmorton Avenue and, farther west, William Street run down it. Spring Street and Wallace Street run diagonally across the lower left, enclosing blocks 6 and 3 with narrow lots, and Linden Place joins Spring Street at the lower left. Blocks 7, 8, 10, 11, 12 and 13 are largely open ground, with rows of dwellings along Mc Laren Street and John Street. Water pipes of 4, 6, 8 and 10 inches are lettered in the streets, and street widths of 30 to 60 feet are given. Neighbouring sheets are numbered 5 and 6 at the left, 34 at the right, 30 at the lower left and 45 at the bottom.
notes: East Front east of Spring Street is now River Road.
Mechanic is the modern Mechanic Street; Mc Laren is Mc Laren Street.
William Street is lettered '(Williams)' in parentheses where it runs between Mechanic and Mc Laren Streets, and '(Wallace)' appears in parentheses on Mc Laren Street east of Throckmorton Avenue.
The sheet is turned: the printed north arrow points about 30 degrees right of straight up, and the fit gives a rotation of about 39 degrees.
Red Bank east: Front, Mechanic, McLaren, William; turned about 39 deg. 100 ft.
placenames: North Branch of Shrewsbury River or Navesink River

sheet-34.description: Sheet 34 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch on a turned sheet with the printed north arrow pointing up and to the right. It is titled 'Red Bank & Fairhaven' and carries the borough boundary, a dash-dot line labelled 'Red Bank Borough Limits' and 'Fairhaven' that crosses the sheet diagonally from lower left to upper right. The North Branch of the Shrewsbury River, or Navesink River, runs along the top. Below it long narrow lots belonging to riverside estates, lettered A to M with large frame dwellings, tile-roofed buildings and auto garages, extend down to East Front Street, which crosses the middle of the sheet and continues to the right as Fairhaven Road. Vista Place and Buena Place at the upper left serve block 2, a platted tract of narrow house lots. Harrison Avenue and Lake Avenue run down from East Front Street, Harrison Avenue passing the Mathews Bros. artesian wells and storage yard. At the left edge, High (Smith) Street, Mechanic Street, Worthley Street and Marion Street enclose small blocks 4 and 5 of frame dwellings, with a stretch marked 'Not Opened'. At the lower right, Glen Place and Forest Avenue bound block 9, a subdivision of narrow lots, beside a pond on the right edge. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 18 inches are lettered, the 18-inch main being that of the Fairhaven Manor Water Company. Sheet 33 adjoins on the left, 35 above right and 36 at right.
notes: East Front is the modern River Road west of Lake Avenue; the same road is lettered Fairhaven Road east of it.
High (Smith) is now High Street.
Forest Avenue is Forrest Avenue today and is not used for control: its junctions with Glen Place and Beekman Place did not agree with the fit.
The fit rotation of about 39 degrees differs from the 31 to 32 degrees of sheets 35 to 40; the sheet is drawn at its own angle.
Red Bank / Fairhaven line; turned about 39 deg (7 deg off sheets 35-40). 100 ft.
placenames: North Branch of Shrewsbury River or Navesink River

sheet-35.description: Sheet 35 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and is headed Fairhaven. It shows the north bank of the Navesink River, or North Branch of the Shrewsbury River, which enters the sheet from the upper right and sweeps down the left side to a branch and a large pond at the lower left. Most of the sheet is open ground and large estates. Two long straight streets, Grange Avenue and Hance Road, run from the top of the sheet to Fairhaven Road along the bottom edge. Between them lie a few scattered frame dwellings, stables and garages, and east of Hance Road the estate of A. F. Lichenstein, with a dwelling, windmill and elevated tank, auto garages and hen houses. West of Grange Avenue a pond with an ice house and the buildings of an estate stand on the shore of the river. At the lower left Lake Avenue enters the corner of the sheet, beside the line marking the Red Bank borough and Fairhaven township limits. At the bottom edge Fairhaven Road is drawn with its water pipes of 6 and 18 inches, and the heads of Chestnut Street, Lincoln Avenue and Lexington Street appear just below it. The sheet is turned, with its north arrow pointing up and to the right. Sheets 34 and 36 border it below left and below, and sheet 37 lies to the right.
notes: Fairhaven Road is the modern East Front Street.
Only Grange Avenue and Hance Road meet Fairhaven Road within the drawn part, so the part is placed by a helmert transformation from two junctions on one street and has low confidence.
Lexington Street is Lexington Avenue today, and it meets Fairhaven Road close to Grange Avenue.
Fairhaven west, river; two junctions (helmert). 100 ft.
placenames: Navesink River or North Branch of the Shrewsbury River

sheet-36.description: Sheet 36 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and is headed Fairhaven. It covers the southern part of the village of Fairhaven below Fairhaven Road, which runs along the top edge of the sheet. The built-up part is a gridded subdivision of about nine numbered blocks lying between Chestnut Street, drawn as a diagonal road from the upper left, and Hance Road at the right. Lincoln Avenue and Lexington Avenue run down from Fairhaven Road, crossed by 1st Street, 2nd Street and Poplar Street, and the blocks hold frame dwellings with garages on lots lettered A to L. Block 7 is a long strip of narrow platted lots with almost no buildings, and block 12 at the bottom is open ground. On the left a long pond, block 8, lies between Chestnut Street and Forest Avenue, with a creek running from its lower end. Glen Place and Beekman Place cross Forest Avenue at the left edge. At the right edge Cherry Lane, Parker Avenue, Jackson Street and 3rd Street join Hance Road, and a compass rose stands beside them. A dash-dot line near the bottom edge marks a limit line with sheet 51. Street widths of 30, 40, 45, 50 and 55 feet and water pipes of 6 and 18 inches are lettered. The sheet is turned, with its north arrow pointing up and to the right.
notes: Fairhaven Road is the modern East Front Street; Chestnut, Lincoln Avenue, Lexington Avenue and Poplar are Chestnut Street, Lincoln Avenue, Lexington Avenue and Poplar Avenue.
Forest Avenue is Forrest Avenue today; its junctions with Glen Place and Beekman Place were rejected by the fit (9 and 19 m) and are not used.
Fairhaven: Fairhaven Rd, Poplar; Forrest Av left out (displaced). 100 ft.

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and is headed Fairhaven. It shows the north side of Fairhaven Road, with the Navesink River, or North Branch of the Shrewsbury River, curving across the top of the sheet in a wide bend and the north arrow pointing up and to the right. Hance Road runs the full height of the sheet at the left, with a 4-inch water pipe. East of it lies a series of very long narrow lots stretching from the river to Fairhaven Road, most of them undeveloped and lettered F, G, H and J where a dwelling stands. A private road of the estate at the upper left, partly dashed, runs from Hance Road to the dwellings, and another private road follows the east side of the sheet. A cemetery is marked at the right. At the bottom, along Fairhaven Road, narrow lots A to M hold frame dwellings and auto garages, and at the lower right Navesink Street and Navesink Avenue enclose blocks 4 and 5, where a row of small lots carries dwellings, with Smith Street and Cedar Avenue shown below the road. An 18-inch water main and a fire alarm box mark Fairhaven Road, and the borough limit is lettered at the right edge. Sheet 35 adjoins at the left, 38 at the right and 39 below.
notes: Fairhaven Road is the modern East Front Street.
The detected junction of Navesink Avenue with East Front Street lay 15 m from the drawn Navesink Street and was replaced by a hand-picked point.
The part has four collinear control points along Fairhaven Road and is placed by a helmert transformation: low confidence.
Fairhaven: East Front (Fairhaven Rd) only; collinear points (helmert). 100 ft.
placenames: North Branch of Shrewsbury River or Navesink River

sheet-38.description: Sheet 38 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and is headed Fairhaven. A margin note says that part of this territory is shown on sheet 77 of New Jersey Coast Volume I. The Navesink River, or North Branch of the Shrewsbury River, crosses the upper part of the sheet and turns back to the east; a bulkhead wall is lettered along its south shore, and a pier with a small building projects at the upper right. Fourth Creek, a tidal creek, comes down from the river through the middle of the sheet to Fairhaven Road, dividing the land west of it from block 1 on the east. West of the creek long narrow lots run from the river road to Fairhaven Road, with Battin Road, a street lined with dwellings, along their east side. The shoreline lots at the upper right hold the Grand View Hotel, marked as not open when surveyed, and large estate dwellings. Pearl Avenue runs down the right edge and is crossed by Clay Street and Haggar's Lane. Along Fairhaven Road at the bottom a row of lots numbered 91 to 109 carries small frame dwellings, with Cedar, Locust, Maple and Church Avenues entering from below. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 18 inches are lettered. Sheets 37, 39 and 40 adjoin.
notes: Fairhaven Road is the modern East Front Street, and east of Church Street it is River Road; Pearl Avenue is the modern Fair Haven Road; Church Avenue is Church Street; Haggar's Lane is modern Hagger Lane.
Clay Street's modern junction with Fair Haven Road lay 26 m from the fit and was not used.
Sheet 38 carries a margin note: Part of this territory shown on Sheet 77 New Jersey Coast Vol. I.
Fairhaven: Fairhaven Rd, Maple, Church, Locust; Clay St left out (26 m off); collinear points. 100 ft.
placenames: North Branch of Shrewsbury River or Navesink River

sheet-39.description: Sheet 39 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and is headed Fairhaven. It shows a rectangular grid of mostly undeveloped blocks in the southern part of the village, with Fairhaven Road along the top edge and Navesink Street entering from above. Hance Road runs down the left side of the sheet and Cedar Avenue down the right. Smith Street divides the upper blocks, and Cherry Lane, Parker Avenue, Jackson Street and 3rd Street cross the sheet from left to right, forming blocks 1 to 9. Streets are lettered 33, 40 and 50 feet wide, and water pipes of 4 and 18 inches lie in Fairhaven Road. Most of the blocks are empty, subdivided into long lots lettered A to N, and the buildings are few: a group of frame dwellings and auto garages along the top of block 1, two dwellings in block 3, a coop and dwellings in block 7, and a row of small lots with dwellings, outhouses and coops along 3rd Street in block 8, where the fire alarm box at the corner with Cedar Avenue is marked. Block 9, the largest, holds a few farm buildings with a long outbuilding near Hance Road. At the left edge 1st Street, 2nd Street and Poplar Street end at Hance Road, and Fisk Street and Hendrickson Street enter at the right. A dash-dot line near the bottom is a sheet limit. The sheet is turned, with the north arrow up and to the right.
notes: Fairhaven Road is the modern East Front Street; Smith is Smith Street.
Cherry Lane appears to be the modern Forman Street; it was not used for control.
The junction of Cedar Avenue and Parker Avenue was rejected by the fit (3.8 m).
Fairhaven: Cedar, Parker, Cherry Lane, Fairhaven Rd. 100 ft.

sheet-40.description: Sheet 40 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and is headed Fairhaven. It covers the centre of the village of Fairhaven, with the main street lettered Fairhaven Avenue along the top edge and a margin note that part of block 4 is shown on sheet 77 of New Jersey Coast Volume I. The built-up blocks, 1 to 12, lie between Cedar Avenue at the left and Pearl Avenue at the right, with Locust Avenue, Maple Avenue and Church Avenue running down from the main street, crossed by Fisk, 3rd Street and Hendrickson. Along the main street stand frame dwellings and the Episcopal Church (heated by furnace, lit by electricity), with a fire department building at the upper right carrying a fire bell on a steel tower, a hose house and a gas storage tank. The Fisk Chapel (A.M.E.) and a public school (stove heat, no lighting) lie in block 4, and Jos. Hayes, florist, has glasshouses in block 5. A creek and a pond run across the right-hand block 6 and block 10. Willow Street meets Pearl Avenue at the right; Richardson and William Streets run in the lower left, and Hendrickson and McCarter streets lie across the bottom, where blocks 11 and 12 are platted narrow lots with few buildings. A fire department table of equipment is printed at the upper right. Sheet 38 is above and 39 at the left.
notes: Fairhaven Avenue is the modern East Front Street and, east of Maple Avenue, River Road; Church Avenue is Church Street; Pearl Avenue is Fair Haven Road; Richardson is modern Allen Street; Hendrickson is Hendrickson Place; McCarter is Mc Carter Avenue.
William Street's junction with 3rd Street was rejected by the fit (15.7 m) and William Street is left out of the configuration.
The sheet carries a printed table of fire department equipment at the upper right, and the note 'Part of Block 4 Shown on Sheet 77 N.J. Coast Vol. I.'
Fairhaven centre: Fairhaven Rd, Pearl Av, Hendrickson, McCarter; William St left out. 100 ft.

sheet-41.description: Sheet 41 covers the northwest corner of Fairhaven, on the south shore of the North Branch of the Shrewsbury River or Navesink River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the north arrow tilted toward the upper right. Pearl Avenue runs down the left edge of the sheet and Clay crosses the lower part from Pearl Avenue east past De Normandie Avenue to Gillespie Avenue. De Normandie Avenue and Gillespie Avenue run north from Clay toward the river, and De Normandie Avenue continues south to the bottom edge. The river and its curved shore run diagonally across the top, with a bulkhead lettered along the shore and a boat house at the water's edge. The sheet is lightly built up: frame dwellings with outbuildings stand on large numbered lots along Pearl Avenue and on the blocks either side of De Normandie Avenue, while the ground east of Gillespie Avenue is open apart from a few buildings, among them a house with a round tower near the shore. Block numbers 1 to 5 are lettered, and water pipes of 6 inches with hydrants run in the streets. A note at the upper left states that the river frontage is covered by Sheets 77 and 78 of New Jersey Coast, Volume 1. The adjoining Red Bank sheets are 38 to the west, 44 to the east and 42 to the south.
notes: The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, although the atlas lists sheets 41 to 47 as 100 ft sheets.
Pearl Avenue is the modern Fair Haven Road. Clay is the modern Clay Street.
Placed by three junctions along Clay only, so the placement is a similarity fit (low confidence).
Fairhaven north-west, 50 ft (printed); Clay St only (helmert).
placenames: North Branch of Shrewsbury River or Navesink River

sheet-42.description: Sheet 42 shows the centre of Fairhaven, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north turned toward the upper right. Fairhaven Road, the main street, crosses the sheet from Pearl Avenue at the left edge to the right edge, with water pipes of 18 and 4 inches laid in it. North of it De Normandie Avenue and Gillespie Avenue run up from the road, with Minton Lane and Oak Place meeting it near the right edge, and the blocks between carry frame dwellings, stores and outbuildings on numbered lots. South of the road the sheet shows the Post Office, a church lettered M. E. Church, the Public School and the Atlantic Hotel, with dwellings between them. Willow runs parallel to Fairhaven Road a block to the south, from Pearl Avenue to Oak Place, and the ground south of it is a large unbuilt tract, numbered 2, crossed by a curving road lettered Private Rd. drawn with a dashed pipeline. A dash-dot line lettered A and B marks the bottom edge, where the territory continues on sheet 43. A note at the upper right says the territory is partly covered by Sheets 77 and 78 of New Jersey Coast, Volume 1.
notes: The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, although the atlas lists sheets 41 to 47 as 100 ft sheets.
Fairhaven Road is the modern River Road. Pearl Avenue is the modern Fair Haven Road. Willow is the modern Willow Street. Oak Place and Minton Lane meet Fairhaven Road at one modern junction.
Reading of the larger lettering (Atlantic Hotel, Public School, M. E. Church, Post Office) is from the overview as well as crops.
Fairhaven centre, 50 ft (printed): Fairhaven Rd, Pearl Av, Willow.

sheet-43.description: Sheet 43 shows an almost empty tract on the southern edge of Fairhaven, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north turned toward the upper right. Pearl Avenue runs down the left edge and the sheet is bounded at the top by a dash-dot match line lettered A and B, where it joins sheet 42; neighbouring sheet numbers 42, 44 and 52 are printed around the edge. Almost all of the ground is one large numbered block, 2, belonging to Thos. N. McCarter, with no buildings. A road lettered Private Rd. runs from the top of the sheet southeast across the block as a pair of dashed lines, and a lake with an irregular shore fills the lower left. A north arrow stands near the lake and the scale bar at the bottom reads 50 feet. The only street is Pearl Avenue, whose east edge is drawn along the left side with a water pipe laid in it; no street junction is drawn, so the sheet was placed from a corner of the match line carried from sheet 42 rather than from detected junctions.
notes: The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, although the atlas lists sheets 41 to 47 as 100 ft sheets.
Pearl Avenue is the modern Fair Haven Road.
Placed from one point carried from sheet 42 (Pearl Avenue edge at match line A) with the scale and rotation of sheet 42; low confidence.
Fairhaven south, 50 ft (printed); lake, no junction; anchored on a match-line corner carried from sheet 42.

sheet-44.description: Sheet 44 covers the eastern part of Fairhaven and the edge of Rumson, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north turned toward the upper right. Fairhaven Road crosses the upper part of the sheet from the left edge, bends to the northeast near the middle and runs to the right edge, where Buena Vista Avenue marks the boundary of the Borough of Rumson. North of the road the North Branch of the Shrewsbury River or Navesink River curves across the top, with a small tributary creek running south from it through the sheet. The streets west of the creek form a compact grid of small blocks, numbered 3 to 8, with Oak Place, Elm Place, Willow, Kemp Avenue, Doughty's Lane, Sycamore Place, Lockwood Place, Catherine and Minton Lane, all lined with small frame dwellings. East of the creek the land is mostly open, with the Pentalpha Realty Co. tract at upper right (blocks 9 and 10), a long narrow building and scattered houses. Near the bottom, beside the creek, stands the Rumson Improvement Assn pumping station. A note at the top says part of this territory is shown on Sheet 78 of New Jersey Coast, Volume 1.
notes: Fairhaven Road is the modern River Road. Willow is the modern Willow Street, Sycamore Place is Sycamore Lane, Catherine is Katherine Street, Elm Place and Kemp Avenue are offset across Willow.
Browns Lane / River Road was not used: the modern junction lies about 17 m from where the fit puts the drawn lane.
Reading of the Pentalpha Realty Co. and pumping station lettering is from the overview as well as crops.
Fairhaven east to the Rumson line: Fairhaven Rd (River Road), Oak, Elm, Willow, Buena Vista. 100 ft.
placenames: North Branch of Shrewsbury River or Navesink River
