sheet-45.description: Sheet 45 covers farmland and scattered estates on the boundary between Fairhaven and Little Silver, drawn at 200 feet to an inch with north turned toward the upper right. Prospect Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet and Harrison Avenue (Parker Avenue) lies to the east of it; Harding Road crosses from the upper left in a long curve and runs southeast across both. At the upper left Tower Hill Avenue and Spring meet near the corner of the sheet, and Branch Avenue runs down the left edge to Rumson Road, which closes the bottom of the sheet. A chain line marks the boundary between the Borough of Red Bank and the Borough of Fairhaven. Building is sparse: the Red Bank Reservoir and the U. H. McCarter estate with its drives and grounds lie at the upper centre, with the Tower Hill Farm and M. W. Kennedy and Sons, Florists, near Harding Road, and the A. I. Elkus place at the left. Subdivision lots are laid out at the lower left (blocks 4 and 5) and along Rumson Road; most of the rest is open fields in numbered tracts. A note at the top says part of this territory is shown on Sheet 75 of New Jersey Coast, Volume 1.
notes: The sheet is drawn at 200 feet to an inch, although the atlas lists it as a 100 ft sheet.
Taber is the modern Tabor Street. Harding Road, Tower Hill Avenue and Spring were realigned: the junctions at their west end did not agree with the modern lines and were not used.
Branch Avenue / Rumson Road and Harrison Avenue / Rumson Road lie 15 to 19 m from the drawn junctions and were left out.
Place and street names on the left and top edges are from the overview and crops of limited extent; medium confidence.
Fairhaven and Little Silver, 200 ft (printed); sparse; Harding Rd west end and Branch Av realigned.

sheet-46.description: Sheet 46 shows the Little Silver Station district, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north turned toward the upper right. The railroad runs diagonally from the upper left to the lower right in a multi-track corridor, with the station building and freight yard beside it near the middle left. Branch Avenue and Oceanport Avenue run along the west side of the tracks, and Willow Drive curves up from them past Parker Avenue to meet Little Silver Point Road at the top of the sheet. East of the tracks the sheet is laid out in subdivisions of long narrow numbered lots: the tract along Little Silver Point Road and Parker Avenue at the upper right, a larger tract between Parker Avenue and Eastview Avenue, and a grid of blocks lettered 3 to 10 bounded by Eastview Avenue, Silverside Avenue, Riverview Avenue and Edgewood Avenue, with Conover Place curving through the southern block. Dwellings are few and scattered. At the lower left a long group of greenhouses belongs to Dean and Co. Florists. A label at the upper right reads Little Silver Station.
notes: Sycamore is the modern Sycamore Avenue. The modern Branch Avenue / Eastview Avenue / Oceanport Avenue node was not detected.
The railroad is the North Jersey Coast Line; its crossing of Silverside Avenue is one of the control points.
Little Silver Station: Willow Dr, Sycamore, Oceanport, Silverside; drawn at its own angle (24 deg). 100 ft.

sheet-47.description: Sheet 47 covers the Little Silver section south of Rumson Road, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north turned toward the upper right. Rumson Road runs across the top, Branch Avenue down the left edge and Prospect Avenue down the right edge, with Markham Place crossing the middle from Branch Avenue to Prospect Avenue and Lovett Avenue running south from it. At the bottom Willow Drive curves across the lower right. A stream runs from the middle of the sheet to the lower right. The ground is mostly open fields in large numbered tracts, with a row of small dwellings on lots along Rumson Road at the upper left and a larger group of greenhouses for Winfield White, Florist, just south of it. C. W. Schneider, Florist, has a further group of greenhouses and a dwelling near the middle of the sheet. A public school lies on Prospect Avenue near the right edge, with small lots along its frontage, and lots are laid out on the north side of Markham Place and along the south side of the stream. Sheet 45 adjoins at the top, and a note refers to sheet 75 of New Jersey Coast, Volume 1.
notes: Branch Avenue / Rumson Road and Branch Avenue / Markham Place lie 7 to 9 m from the drawn junctions in the fit and were left out; the placement rests on three junctions and has no spare control.
Reading of the greenhouse owners and the school label is from the overview as well as crops.
Little Silver: Prospect, Rumson Rd, Markham; Branch Av left out (displaced). Three points. 100 ft.

sheet-48.description: Sheet 48 shows the Little Silver Section on the Red Bank and Little Silver boundary, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Rumson Road forms the top edge and Kings Avenue the bottom edge, with Prospect Avenue along the left edge and Seven Bridge Road along the right edge. Church Street crosses the upper left diagonally from Prospect Avenue to Rumson Road, lettered with a 4 inch water pipe. Almost all of the built-up area lies along it and in the upper left corner. Dwellings, sheds and coops line both sides of Church Street, with a squab farm in the top left corner. Between them stand Embury M.E. Church and its church hall beside a cemetery, a hall, a building marked as a post office, and the Little Silver Fire Company No. 2 station, with a note listing its American LaFrance motor truck, pump capacity and hose. Below the road is J. T. Lovett's nursery with long greenhouses. Beyond Church Street the sheet is mostly large unbuilt, numbered tracts, with a few farm buildings and one house near the right edge. A short street north of Rumson Road is lettered Harrison Street, and a street near the right edge is lettered (Not Named). A small stream crosses the right edge. Compass roses and the sheet numbers of the neighbouring sheets are printed in the margins: 45 above, 47 to the left, 50 below and 53 to the right. A note at the top says that part of this territory is shown on Sheet 75, New Jersey Coast, Volume 1.
notes: Church is today Church Street; Kings Avenue is Kings Road; Seven Bridge Road is Seven Bridges Road; Harrison Street is Harrison Avenue.
Prospect Avenue is drawn 60 to 85 feet wide with a jog at Church Street, so the three points placed on it carry residuals of 1.6 to 4.7 m.
A street near the right edge is lettered (Not Named) and has no modern counterpart in the street data.
Scale 100 feet to an inch; the sheet is turned so that north is about 37 degrees clockwise from straight up.
Little Silver section: Church St, Rumson Rd, Prospect Av. 100 ft.

sheet-49.description: Sheet 49 covers the Little Silver Section south and west of Prospect Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Prospect Avenue runs down the right edge and Little Silver Point Road along the bottom. Willow Drive crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the upper right, where it curves into Prospect Avenue near Kings Road, and then runs straight down the left side of the sheet. Lovett Avenue joins Willow Drive from the north, drawn 40 feet wide, and Parker Avenue runs south from Little Silver Point Road. A brook crosses the middle of the sheet and leaves it at the lower right, with a tributary and a second small stream at the upper left and upper right. Most of the sheet is large unbuilt tracts, divided by lot lines into numbered lots. The only compact development is a row of small lots with houses, coops and sheds on the east side of Willow Drive near the top, facing Prospect Avenue; a few farm buildings stand on the larger tracts, and a small group of houses, coops and a gasoline tank lies at the left edge. Block numbers and the sheet numbers of the neighbouring sheets are printed in the margins: 47 above, 71 and 46 on the left, 50 to the right and 46 below. A faint ghost of sheet 48 shows at the top.
notes: Parker Avenue is today Parker Road.
The modern Prospect Avenue and Little Silver Point Road junction lies about 40 m from the drawn one; it was excluded.
The Prospect Avenue and Willow Drive junction at the top right coincides with Kings Road and could not be placed reliably; the part rests on three points.
Scale 100 feet to an inch; the sheet is turned so that north is about 36 degrees clockwise from straight up.
Little Silver: Willow Drive, Prospect; three points. 100 ft.

sheet-50.description: Sheet 50 shows the east side of Little Silver, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Kings Avenue runs along the top, Prospect Avenue down the left edge, Seven Bridge Road down the right edge and Little Silver Point Road along the bottom. A heading in the top right corner gives Little Silver and the scale. The upper part is a set of long, narrow numbered tracts running north and south from Kings Avenue, almost all unbuilt, with a single house and garage in the top left corner. A brook enters at the left edge, runs diagonally across the sheet and joins Little Silver Creek, which widens to the right with a tidal inlet and leaves at the right edge. A group of small lots, numbered 14 to 18, with houses faces Prospect Avenue below the brook, and further houses, barns and a corn crib stand on the large tract to the west. On the east side are a house with outbuildings, a garage and a small gasoline engine. St. John's Chapel, lit by electricity and heated by furnace, stands on a small lot opposite Little Silver Point Road at the bottom. Compass roses are drawn at the lower left and right. The neighbouring sheets are printed in the margins: 48 above, 49 to the left, 53 to the right, 55 to the lower right, and a lower sheet below.
notes: Kings Avenue is today Kings Road; Seven Bridge Road is Seven Bridges Road.
The modern Prospect Avenue and Little Silver Point Road junction lies about 40 m from the drawn one; it was excluded.
The detector paired Kings Avenue with the heading box at the top right, so the Kings Avenue and Seven Bridge Road junction was hand-picked.
Scale 100 feet to an inch; the sheet is turned so that north is about 38 degrees clockwise from straight up.
Little Silver: Kings Av to Little Silver Point Rd; three points. 100 ft.

sheet-51.description: Sheet 51 shows the open country between Little Silver, Fairhaven and Rumson, drawn at 200 feet to an inch (the atlas list gives 100) and turned so that north points to the upper right. Ridge Road runs from the left edge to the right edge across the upper half, with the boundary line between Fairhaven and the Borough of Rumson drawn along it. Hance Road crosses it from the top edge to Rumson Road near the bottom, with the boundary between Shrewsbury Township and the Borough of Rumson along its southern part. Harding Road curves in from the left edge and runs down to Rumson Road, which crosses the bottom of the sheet, and Seven Bridge Road leaves it at the lower left. The sheet is almost entirely unbuilt, divided into a few numbered tracts. Buildings appear only near the bottom: the Rumson Riding School, a house marked Chas. P. Doelger, L. J. Ryan, C. P. Doelger and J. Horace Harding, with small farm buildings. A short Private Road leaves Rumson Road at the lower right, near a stream. At the top right Hendrickson Street leaves the road lettered Mc Carter and Maple Avenue is lettered at the right edge. A dash-dot match line with lettered corners A to D runs across the top. The sheet numbers of the neighbouring sheets are printed: 36, 39 and 40 above, 45 to the left, 52 to the right and 53 below.
notes: Seven Bridge Road is today Seven Bridges Road; Hance Avenue south of Rumson Road is part of today's Hance Road.
The modern Hance Road and Rumson Road junction lies about 57 m from the drawn one; it was excluded.
The printed scale is 200 feet to an inch, so the config sets scale_ft 200; the atlas list says 100.
Hendrickson Street and Maple Avenue are lettered near the top right edge, mostly drawn on sheet 52.
Fairhaven, Rumson and Shrewsbury Township, 200 ft (printed): Harding Rd, Ridge Rd, Hance Av.

sheet-52.description: Sheet 52 covers the northern part of Rumson and the Fairhaven line, drawn at 200 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Ridge Road crosses the middle of the sheet from left to right, with the boundary line between the Borough of Fairhaven and the Borough of Rumson drawn along it, and Rumson Road crosses the bottom. Pearl Avenue and Kemp Avenue run north and south across both roads, Buena Vista Avenue runs down the right edge, and McCarter and Maple Avenue lie at the upper left, with Hendrickson Street leaving McCarter. Conover Street runs south from Rumson Road at the bottom, and a Private Road runs off Rumson Road at lower left and at the right. The sheet is largely large estates. At the centre are the buildings of the Thos. N. McCarter estate along Pearl Avenue, including a pink-coloured fireproof building and a note on hose kept on a reel. On the right are the estates of Geo. V. Coe and others, with several duck ponds. Further McCarter property and a group of houses lie at the lower left. A small lake and stream run in at the top. A note says parts of this territory are shown on Sheet 84, New Jersey Coast, Volume 1, and the right margin refers to New Jersey Coast Maps Volume One.
notes: Pearl Avenue is today Fair Haven Road north of Ridge Road and Fairhaven Road south of it; Conover Street is Conover Lane.
The fit has an RMSE of 5.7 m with 7 points: Ridge Road and Rumson Road junctions differ by 4 to 8 m from the drawn ones.
The printed scale is 200 feet to an inch, so the config sets scale_ft 200; the atlas list says 100.
Fairhaven and Rumson, 200 ft (printed): Ridge Rd, Rumson Rd, Pearl Av.

sheet-53.description: Sheet 53 shows the southern Rumson district between the Little Silver boundary and Rumson Park, drawn at 200 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Rumson Road crosses the top edge, with Harding Road leaving it at the upper left and Seven Bridge Road running down the left side, crossing Little Silver Creek at the bottom. A Kings Road stub leaves Seven Bridge Road from the west. Hance Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet with the boundary between Shrewsbury Township and the Borough of Rumson drawn along its length. A Private Road with fire hydrants runs down the right side beside Rumson Park, curving to the right at the bottom. Two streams run from Rumson Road to Little Silver Creek, one at the left and one at the right, and the creek, with its tidal branches, crosses the lower half with a boundary line drawn along it. The sheet is nearly all farmland and estates, with the houses of a few named owners, water tanks, outbuildings and a small pond. The neighbouring sheet numbers are printed: 51 at the top, 48 and 50 on the left, 54 on the right, 55 and 56 below.
notes: Seven Bridge Road is today Seven Bridges Road; Hance Avenue is part of today's Hance Road.
The part rests on three points close to Seven Bridges Road; the far side of the sheet is unchecked.
The printed scale is 200 feet to an inch, so the config sets scale_ft 200; the atlas list says 100.
Rumson and Shrewsbury Township, 200 ft (printed): Seven Bridge Rd; three points.

sheet-54.description: Sheet 54 covers the Rumson Park and Rumson Country Club grounds and the Buena Vista Avenue frontage, drawn at 200 feet to an inch (the scale bar says 100, but the street spacing fits 200) and turned so that north points to the upper right. Rumson Road runs along the top from the left edge to the upper right, with Pearl Avenue, Kemp Avenue, Conover and Buena Vista Avenue meeting it, and a Private Road leaving it at the left, running down the west side of Rumson Park and continuing across the sheet as a curving road to the club house. The central area is Rumson Park, with golf links, polo grounds and polo field stables, and a note on the Rumson Country Club listing its electric light, steam heat and the water supply from two Goulds pumps and the water tanks. The red club house stands on the Shrewsbury River shore at the bottom, with a country club wharf at the right. Conover runs south from Rumson Road along the east side, bordered by large named estates and a cemetery. A duck pond and streams reach Rumson Road at the top right. Water pipes are drawn throughout. A note says part of this territory is shown on Sheet 84, New Jersey Coast, Volume 1; the right margin refers to New Jersey Coast Maps Volume One.
notes: Conover is today Conover Lane; the Private Road at the left is today Club Way.
All five points lie along Rumson Road, so rotation rests on the bends of that road: low confidence.
The printed scale bar says 100 feet to an inch while the heading says 200; the street spacing fits 200.
Rumson Park and country club, 200 ft (header; bar says 100); points along Rumson Rd only.

sheet-55.description: Sheet 55 shows Little Silver Point, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Seven Bridge Road runs down the left edge, crossing Middle Creek at the bottom. Little Silver Point Road leaves it at the upper left and runs diagonally to the right edge, where it passes Battle Row at the lower right. Little Silver Creek runs across the top and right of the sheet and Middle Creek across the bottom, with tidal marsh in the lower left. North of the road are narrow numbered lots running down to the creek, with a few houses, garages and sheds. South of the road, the large tract 2 occupies most of the sheet and is unbuilt apart from a house and garage on a small lot beside the road. At the right edge, Battle Row is lined with dwellings and sheds and a pink-coloured house, among small lots running to the south-east. A boat house stands on the creek at the top left. The numbers of the neighbouring sheets are printed: 53 above, 50 at the left, 56 at the right. The Little Silver Point heading and the scale are in the top left corner. Block numbers 1, 2 and 3 are drawn on the large tracts.
notes: Seven Bridge Road is today Seven Bridges Road; Battle Row has no counterpart in the street data.
The part rests on one measured point (Seven Bridges Road and Little Silver Point Road) plus a derived point: low confidence.
Little Silver Point, 100 ft; Little Silver Point Rd, Battle Row; anchored on one junction.

sheet-56-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 56 continues the Little Silver Point sheets eastward, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Little Silver Point Road runs diagonally from the upper left to the lower right, between Little Silver Creek along the top and Middle Creek along the bottom. At the left edge Battle Row leaves the road toward Middle Creek, lined with small numbered lots, dwellings, sheds, garages and a few outbuildings, and a narrow lane of lots runs parallel to the road south of it. Along both sides of Little Silver Point Road the land is divided into long numbered lots running back to the creeks, with scattered dwellings, garages and barns, and a large vacant dwelling near the upper left. Blocks 1 and 3 are numbered on either side of the road. The creeks are drawn with their marsh edges, and Little Silver Creek and Middle Creek are lettered across the sheet. A wedge-shaped inset bordered by a heavy line on the right side of the sheet (part 2) shows the end of the point and is not part of this mask. The sheet notes that the area is shown also on sheet 76 of the New Jersey Coast volume 1.
notes: Battle Row is today Borden Place (by direction and position).
Anchored on the Borden Place / Little Silver Point Road junction with scale assumed (3.97 px/ft) and rotation from the measured lines; low confidence.
Shown also on Sheet 76, N.J. Coast Vol. 1.
Little Silver Point, 100 ft. Main map (part 1: Little Silver Point Rd, Battle Row = Borden Place) and a wedge-shaped inset (part 2) with the east end of the road and the creeks.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: wedge-shaped inset: east end of Little Silver Point Road between Little Silver Creek and Middle Creek (no street junction; the drawn road end is not a reliable match for the modern road end; needs parcel corners (locate.py corner) or the N.J. Coast vol. 1 sheet 76).

sheet-57.description: Sheet 57 shows open farmland in Shrewsbury Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north turned slightly clockwise of the page. Shrewsbury Avenue runs down the left edge of the sheet, with only its east side drawn, and Patterson Avenue crosses the sheet from left to right about a third of the way down, lettered 70 feet wide. The main line of the Central Railroad of New Jersey runs north to south across the whole sheet in a corridor of parallel lines, crossing Patterson Avenue at a grade crossing and bending slightly to the south-west towards the foot of the sheet. North of Patterson Avenue the sheet is almost blank: it carries only numbered plots and block numbers 11, 12, 13, 26 and 27, with the match line to sheet 59 near the top. South of Patterson Avenue a few frame dwellings and outbuildings stand beside the avenue and the railroad, and a row of narrow lots numbered 21 to 27 lies at the right edge, next to Patterson Avenue. Shadow Brook crosses the lower half from the railroad towards the right edge. Near the bottom right a farm building group is labelled Shadow Brook Farm, owner Dr. Ernest Fahnestock, with a note to see sheet 58 for the report, and a six inch water pipe runs east from it. A dash-dot match line with the letters A and B runs along the bottom edge below the number 59. The compass rose at the upper left is turned a few degrees from the page edge. Most of the sheet is unbuilt, and only the two street edges and the railroad give control.
notes: Only two junctions are usable on this sheet (Patterson Avenue with Shrewsbury Avenue and with the railroad), so the placement is a helmert fit.
The railroad is the modern Southern Secondary line.
Shrewsbury Township: Patterson Av, Shrewsbury Av, railroad; two points (helmert). 100 ft.

sheet-58.description: Sheet 58 covers the Shrewsbury section along Broad Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Broad Street runs from top to bottom a little to the right of centre of the sheet, with a six inch and an eight inch water pipe lettered in it. Thomas Avenue forms the top of the sheet on the west side of Broad Street and carries a row of narrow numbered lots 1 to 19 along its south side, while White Road leaves Broad Street towards the east just below it. Patterson Avenue, 70 feet wide, crosses the sheet at about a quarter of its height. South of Patterson Avenue a re-subdivision of Lot 17 shows lots on both sides of two short 35 foot streets, Trenton and Newark. East of Broad Street, Monroe Avenue and North Monroe Avenue are laid out with a long row of lots numbered 77 to 107. Shadow Brook comes in from the left edge, rises towards Broad Street and crosses beneath it. The lower half of the sheet is the Shadow Brook Farm, owner Dr. Ernest Fahnestock, with a long note on hydrants, hose and chemical extinguishers, drawn with a stable, hay barn, coops, carriage house and several dwellings in yellow, and a six inch water pipe crossing the sheet east to west near the bottom. The right-hand half is mostly unbuilt. A compass rose stands at the upper right, the scale bar is at the lower left, and the match line to sheet 60 runs along the foot of the sheet. Adjoining sheets are 57 at the left, 71 at the right and 60 below.
notes: Trenton and Newark are drawn here as streets between Patterson Avenue and the farm land; the modern streets on the same lines are Allen Street and Glorney Street, which the fit supports.
White is printed as White Road and meets Broad Street opposite the east end of Thomas Avenue.
Broad Street, Thomas Avenue, White Road, Monroe Avenue and North Monroe Avenue match modern streets with the same names.
Shrewsbury section: Broad, Thomas, Patterson, Monroe, N Monroe, White Rd; Trenton and Newark (Allen and Glorney Streets). 100 ft.

sheet-59.description: Sheet 59 shows the Shrewsbury district west of Broad Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Shrewsbury Avenue runs down the left edge, with only its east side drawn, and Sycamore Avenue crosses the foot of the sheet from left to right, sloping gently down to the east. The Central Railroad of New Jersey runs from top to bottom across the sheet in a parallel-line corridor that narrows and widens twice, and crosses Sycamore Avenue at the bottom beside the Shrewsbury freight station. The block west of the railroad is large and almost empty, apart from a cluster of buildings near the bottom left belonging to the Shrewsbury Dairy Co., with hen houses, a wagon shed, a filling room and an office. Further south, on the other side of Sycamore Avenue, are a few small dwellings, stores, a vacant building and an auto building. East of the railroad stand large farm parcels numbered 2, 31, 32 and 33 with scattered dwellings, barns, hen houses and auto sheds, and a brook enters from the right edge near the right-hand end. A dash-dot match line with the letters B and C runs near the top, below the sheet number 57. The compass rose at the upper left is turned a few degrees clockwise from the page. The match lines and block numbers show that sheet 57 adjoins at the top, 60 at the right and 61 at the right of the foot.
notes: Only two points were hand-picked, Shrewsbury Avenue with Sycamore Avenue and the railroad with Sycamore Avenue; the placement is a helmert fit and low confidence.
The detector could not measure either junction, so both are placed by hand.
The railroad is the modern Southern Secondary line.
Shrewsbury: Shrewsbury Av, Sycamore Av, railroad; two hand-picked points (helmert). 100 ft.

sheet-60.description: Sheet 60 is the centre of the village of Shrewsbury, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Broad Street runs from top to bottom a little left of the middle of the sheet, with an eight inch water pipe and hydrants along it, and Sycamore Avenue crosses the foot of the sheet. White Street branches east from Broad Street near the top, with house lots numbered 15 to 58 along its south side and a row of lots 60 to 76 along its north side. On the west side of Broad Street are the Shrewsbury Public School, a pink brick building, and a series of long narrow parcels numbered 1 to 14 running down to Sycamore Avenue. A brook crosses the sheet from the west edge, runs to Broad Street near the middle and reappears on the east side, flowing off to the right edge. East of Broad Street are the Shrewsbury Hose Co. No. 1 with its fire department building, a Post Office at the corner of Sycamore Avenue, several pink brick dwellings, and the cemetery near the foot. Sycamore Avenue bends at Broad Street and its east part rises towards the right edge. The match lines with letters C and D run along the top of the sheet, and the compass rose is at the right. Sheet 58 adjoins at the top, 59 at the left, 61 below and 71 at the right.
notes: White is the modern White Street east of Broad Street, which meets Obre Place west of it.
Only two junctions (Broad Street with Sycamore Avenue and with White Street) are used, so the placement is a helmert fit along one street.
Shrewsbury village: Broad, Sycamore Av, White; two points on Broad (helmert). 100 ft.

sheet-61.description: Sheet 61 shows Broad Street south of the village of Shrewsbury, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Broad Street runs from the upper right of the sheet to the lower left, 66 feet wide. Sycamore Avenue crosses the top of the sheet, with the numbers 178 to 230 of its lots along its edges and an eight inch water pipe in it. On the east side of Broad Street, near Sycamore Avenue, are Christ Church and its cemetery, a parish house, the Presbyterian Church with its cemetery, and large lots with dwellings, among them a house named Shadyside in quotation marks. West of Broad Street are a few large parcels with dwellings, a kennels building and auto sheds, and much of the sheet is blank. A pond with a stream through it lies at the bottom left, close to the sheet edge, and is repeated on sheet 62. The compass rose is near the upper left, with the sheet number 59 at the left and 71 at the right, and the match line with letters A and B runs along the foot of the sheet. The dwellings are drawn with their outbuildings,. The sheet is drawn with the street at an angle, so the rotation is about 8 degrees against the 6 degrees of sheets 57 to 60.
notes: Broad Street is the only street drawn at length, so the placement is a helmert fit along one street.
A second control point was set on the modern Broad Street centre line at the same scale as sheet 60.
Broad Street south of Sycamore Av; pond. One detected point and one on Broad (helmert). 100 ft.

sheet-62.description: Sheet 62 shows Broad Street where it leaves Shrewsbury and reaches Lafetra's Brook, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Broad Street runs diagonally from the top, where it crosses a pond and brook shared with sheet 61, to the lower left, where the 66 foot street becomes the 80 foot Main. Shrewsbury Avenue enters at the left edge and meets Broad Street near the foot, with a few small house lots numbered 1 to 3 between the two. Meadow Brook Farm fills the upper left with long barns, stables, kennels, a water tank, a dwelling and cribs. East of Broad Street are large farm parcels and a few houses, one with tile roof and stucco finish. Lafetra's Brook crosses the foot of the sheet from the left edge to the right, with the township line lettered along it: Shrewsbury Township to the north and Eatontown Township to the south. A pond is at the top near the sheet number, and a brook runs across the top right. The compass rose is on the right edge. Sheet 61 adjoins at the top, 64 at the foot and 71 at the right.
notes: Only one point could be placed by hand, so this part is anchored and low confidence.
Shrewsbury Avenue is drawn running north-west from Main street here, but the modern Shrewsbury Avenue is aligned differently, so it was left out.
The position of the pond bar was taken from sheet 61 and moved so that the modern Broad Street centre line lies on the drawn street.
Broad, Main, Shrewsbury Av, Lafetra's Brook; anchored on one hand-picked point. 100 ft.

sheet-63.description: Sheet 63 covers the western edge of the village of Eatontown, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Tinton Avenue runs along the top edge, with 4-inch water pipe lettered in it, and Station Road runs south from it to Lewis Street at the left. Between them two blocks of small frame dwellings, numbered 15 to 25 and 101 to 110, face each other across Corporation Row and Mill, both marked arbitrary. The double track of the Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the sheet from the lower left corner to the top edge, with a switch line curving off to the east, and the railroad passenger station stands at the lower left beside Lewis Street. West Street follows the railroad along the right edge. Wampum Brook crosses the middle of the sheet in the east and a smaller stream and ditch cross the west. Along Lewis Street the Gulf Refining Company has a plant for oils and gasoline with an automobile garage and storage tanks, and a large vacant building lettered Harry E. Powers stands south of the tracks beside Pine Brook Road. The southeast corner is laid out in narrow lots between Maple Avenue and High Street, with scattered dwellings and a few outbuildings; most of the ground west of the railroad and north of Tinton Avenue is open farmland marked only with block numbers 1 to 7. A compass is drawn at upper right. The adjoining sheets are 64 to the north east, 66 to the east and 65 to the south.
notes: Lewis is Lewis Street, Maple Av. is Maple Avenue, High is High Street, Corlies Av. is Corlies Avenue and Tinton Av. is Tinton Avenue today.

Corporation Row and Mill are marked arbitrary and do not exist today; Station Road survives only partly, probably as Maxwell Road, but its modern line is about 20 m from the drawn one and was not used.

Pine Brook Road meets Lewis Street about 9 m from its modern junction; the modern Corlies Avenue and High Street junction is not where the sheet draws the bend of High Street and Corlies Avenue, and was left out.
Placed from two junctions on Lewis Street with scale and rotation assumed (helmert): low confidence.
Eatontown west: Lewis, Maple, High; two points (anchored config). 100 ft.

sheet-64.description: Sheet 64 shows the northern edge of Eatontown at 100 feet to an inch. Main Street, 66 feet wide with house numbers from 201 to 257, runs from a fork at the top of the sheet, where Shrewsbury Avenue and Broad Street diverge, south to its junction with Tinton Avenue at lower left and on to the southeast edge of the sheet. Tinton Avenue crosses the lower left corner with 4-inch water pipe lettered in it. Along the top of the sheet Lafetra's Creek, drawn as a broad tinted stream, forms the boundary line between Shrewsbury Township to the north and Eatontown Township to the south. Wampum Brook enters at lower right and a pond with its stream lies at the bottom, close to the sheet 66 edge. Almost all the sheet is open land numbered as blocks 1, 2 and 4: a group of frame dwellings and farm buildings stands on the west side of Main Street and around the Tinton Avenue corner, with a garage and a water tower note giving its elevation, and a few outbuildings. East of the road a row of farm buildings and hen houses lies near the brook. The large blank area at the right belongs to neighbouring sheets 71 and 67, whose numbers are printed at the margin. A compass is drawn at the right.
notes: Main is Main Street, Tinton Av. is Tinton Avenue, Shrewsbury Av. is Shrewsbury Avenue and Broad St. is Broad Street today.
The drawn Main Street north of Tinton Avenue differs from the modern Main Street, which bends away to the east, so only the Main Street and Tinton Avenue junction was used.
Anchored on one junction with the scale and rotation assumed (helmert): low confidence.
Eatontown, Main Street north end, Lafetra's Creek; anchored on Main / Tinton. 100 ft.

sheet-65.description: Sheet 65 covers the southwest side of Eatontown village, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. South Street runs down the right side of the sheet and bends southeast beyond the middle, where Locust Avenue leaves it. At the top Corlies Avenue and Clinton cross South Street and Johnson, and Wolcott is an arbitrary street between Clinton and Buttonwood or Wayside. Maple Avenue runs southeast from the top left corner past the north end of Buttonwood or Wayside. Grant Drive runs down the left side from Buttonwood or Wayside to the bottom, crossing Richardson Avenue and Revey Place, while Thompson, marked arbitrary, runs south from Revey Place. Frame dwellings stand along the streets in blocks 1, 2, 6, 7 and 3, with a group of greenhouses between Johnson and South Street in block 2, and a large block 4 is almost empty. In the southeast a stream runs between South Street and Locust Avenue; Church Street runs along it past the primary school for colored children, and the Mt. Zion African M.E. Church stands on Locust Avenue. A compass is drawn at the left. The adjoining sheets are 63 to the northwest and 66 to the northeast.
notes: Johnson is Franklin Avenue today; Buttonwood or Wayside is Buttonwood Avenue; Grant Drive is Grant Avenue; South is South Street; Locust Av. is Locust Street at least in part.
Wolcott and Thompson are marked arbitrary and have no modern equivalent.
The modern Maple Avenue, Buttonwood Avenue (west part), Grant Avenue, Church Street and Locust Street lie 20 to 30 m from the drawn lines and were not used for control.
The name Church is printed on the short street at lower right; its suffix, if any, was not read.
Eatontown south-west: South St, Clinton, Corlies, Buttonwood; Maple, Grant, Church, Locust left out (20-30 m off). 100 ft.

sheet-66.description: Sheet 66 shows the centre of Eatontown at 100 feet to an inch. Main runs from top to the middle of the sheet and meets Broadway; south of Broadway it continues as South, curving southwest to Corlies Avenue at the bottom left. The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the sheet east and west with a coal yard and sheds, and Railroad Avenue and West run along its two sides. Lewis, a street of small houses, runs west from Main below the railroad, and White runs south from Broadway at the right edge. Along Main Street and Broadway stand the commercial buildings of the village: the hall and fire department with court and school rooms on the third floor, John Hall, the first national bank, a hardware store, a printing and electrical shop, a clothing factory, an auto service station and repair garage, the post office, Masonic Hall, and the M.E., Roman Catholic and Advent churches. Robert Higginson and Son, building supplies and coal, and Henry Allen, coal and feed, stand beside the tracks. A lumber yard fills the north. Wampum Brook crosses the top left. Twin Brooks Farm lies in the open southeast, and a list of the Eatontown Fire Department apparatus is printed at the top right. A compass is drawn at the lower right.
notes: Railroad Av. is Throckmorton Avenue today, Broadway is Broad Street, Lewis is Lewis Street, South is South Street, Willow is Willow Street, Johnson St. is Franklin Avenue and West is West Street.
Broad Street west of Main Street and the modern Lewis and Broad Street junction are not drawn on the sheet and were excluded.
Railroad Av. is drawn narrower than the modern Throckmorton Avenue and both of its junctions sit 2 to 5 m off in the fit.
Drawn scale fits at about 4.08 px per ft, 2.5 percent above the other sheets.
Eatontown centre: Main, Broadway (Broad St), Lewis, railroad. 100 ft.

sheet-67.description: Sheet 67 shows the east side of Eatontown, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The Central Railroad of New Jersey runs diagonally across the sheet from lower left to the top, with Railroad Avenue beside it on the south side for the first few blocks. Broadway comes from White at the lower left, passes between the railroad and block 7, and bends east, running along the sheet to College Avenue, also called Monmouth Road, which is drawn along the right edge. Morris Place and Burns Street are short cross streets north and south of Broadway, and White crosses the bottom left corner. Block 7 is built up with dwellings, a few churches and shops, and stores along Broadway. East of the bend the land is mostly open with scattered dwellings in blocks 8 and 9, and a group of narrow lots with a few houses lies at the upper right on College Avenue between it and Charlevoix Place, which is marked arbitrary. A private road runs along the right edge, with Private Road also marked at the bottom right. Wampum Brook crosses the upper left. A compass is drawn at upper left. The adjoining sheets are 66 to the west, 64 to the northwest, 71 to the north and 68 to the east.
notes: Railroad Av. is Throckmorton Avenue today, Broadway is Broad Street, Morris Pl. is Kellys Lane, Burns St. is Byrnes Lane and College Av. is College Avenue.
The drawn sheet is turned about 20 degrees counterclockwise from north (the compass arrow points up and left).
Charlevoix Place is marked arbitrary and has no modern equivalent.
The Broad Street and College Avenue junction leans on a 2-arm fit and the part has a leave-one-out error over 10 m: low confidence.
Eatontown, Broadway east of the centre, College Av. 100 ft.

sheet-68-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 68 is the main map of the eastern edge of Eatontown, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Broadway runs from left to right across the middle of the sheet, rising gently to the east with 10-inch water pipe along it. At the left College Avenue, also called Monmouth Road, and Academy Avenue run north from Broadway. Between them is block 1, laid out as narrow lots, and a school of brick, Eatontown Public School No. 1, stands on the south side of block 1 near Broadway. Academy Avenue and Lake Avenue bound a block with The Concourse, a street that bends along a stream and runs northeast from Broadway. Lake Avenue runs north from Broadway and again south of it, with a jog at Broadway, and ends at a street marked Not Named. Locust Avenue runs north from Broadway on the east side of block 4, a block of narrow lots. A few frame houses and outbuildings stand along Broadway and in block 7 east of Locust Avenue; the rest of the sheet is open ground in blocks 2, 3, 5, 6 and 8. A brook crosses the left centre and Private Road runs south along the left edge. A compass is drawn at lower right on the border of the inset, which is mapped separately as part 2 and continues the area south of match line A to B.
notes: Broadway is Broad Street today, College Av. is College Avenue, Lake Av. is Lake Avenue north of Broad Street and Brook Street south of it, and Locust Av. is Locust Avenue.
Academy Av. is probably Nicodemus Avenue today (its modern junction is about 20 m from the drawn one and was not used for control).
All control points lie along Broadway, so the part is a helmert fit and the rotation comes from that one line: low confidence.
The cross street control point at Brook Street and Center Street lay 9.7 m off and was left out.

Eatontown, 100 ft to an inch. Main map (Broadway, College Av (Monmouth Rd), Academy Av, The Concourse, Lake Av, Locust Av) and an inset bottom right continuing south of match line A-B (poultry houses, no streets). Inset placed by the lead.

sheet-68-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 68 is an inset in the lower right corner of the Eatontown sheet, at 100 feet to an inch, continuing the ground south of the dash-dot match line A-B drawn along the bottom of the main map. It shows open land with a group of long frame chicken houses and a few small outbuildings in block 8; no street is drawn in it. The figures 0 mark areas with no buildings, and the sheet number 68 is repeated on the match line.
notes: Anchored on end A of the match line, carried from the main map (part 1), with the main map's scale and rotation; the drawn length of A-B differs between the inset and the main map (about 440 against 570 ft), so the placement is low confidence.

Eatontown, 100 ft to an inch. Main map (Broadway, College Av (Monmouth Rd), Academy Av, The Concourse, Lake Av, Locust Av) and an inset bottom right continuing south of match line A-B (poultry houses, no streets). Inset placed by the lead.

sheet-69.description: Sheet 69 shows the new River Plaza subdivision, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about thirty degrees from the page. Manning, Applegate and Newman streets run down the sheet and are crossed by Carpenter, Foster and West Front streets. Hubbard Avenue forms the east side of the platted area, with Nut Swamp Road coming in from the upper left to join it. Numbered lots, mostly 25 feet wide, are laid out in the blocks and carry blocks 3 to 10, with a few dwellings built, mainly in the blocks near Hubbard Avenue and West Front Street. East of Hubbard Avenue are larger parcels numbered block 9, running down to the North Branch of Shrewsbury River or Navesink River, which bounds the sheet on the right. A creek enters from the upper left, passes round the north of the plan, joins a ditch and flows to the river. At the foot West Front Street runs diagonally to a bridge to Shrewsbury at the lower right. In the lower left corner George Street and May Court meet West Front Street, with the Jersey Coast Laundry, a house, a fire hydrant and drying ovens. Most dwellings are frame with one storey and a half or two. Near the top edge, beside Nut Swamp Road, stand a few farm buildings, with the legend No Exposure.
notes: Applegate, Carpenter, Foster, Hubbard, Manning, Newman and West Front match modern streets with the same names.
George Street was left out of the fit because its junction was about 4 m off the others and worsened the leave-one-out error; May Court was left out because its junction was over 11 m from the fit.
The sheet is rotated about 31 degrees against the page, and the fit rests on nine detected junctions.
River Plaza subdivision, turned about 31 deg; George St and May Ct left out. 100 ft.
placenames: North Branch of Shrewsbury River or Navesink River

sheet-70.description: Sheet 70 shows the hamlet of Tinton Falls, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The sheet is crossed by two roads that meet in the middle: Sycamore Avenue runs up to the upper right edge and Water runs down to the lower left, while Tinton Avenue comes in from the upper left and leaves towards the lower right. Pine Brook enters at the top, runs south through the sheet, passes the S. Bennett grist mill, which is lettered as having no light, no heat and water power, and joins the stream that follows Water, along which the township line is lettered between Atlantic Township and Shrewsbury Township. The buildings are scattered farm and village property: the D. A. Walling Est. distillery with its sheds on Tinton Avenue, J. C. Crawford's slaughter house and dwellings, H. C. Coleman's slaughter house on Sycamore Avenue, a gasoline tank and store near the crossing, a church and the Tinton Falls Public School in the lower right, and many large numbered farm parcels. A triangle of land lies at the junction. The compass rose is at the right edge, and the title Tinton Falls is at the upper right with the scale note.
notes: Only the one central junction of Sycamore Avenue, Tinton Avenue and Water Street is placed, so this part is anchored and low confidence.

The detector could not measure the junction, so it was hand-picked as the crossing of the street centre lines; a trial overlay with a rotation of 8 degrees laid the modern streets on the drawn ones across the sheet.
Water is the modern Water Street.
Tinton Falls: Sycamore Av, Tinton Av, Water St; anchored on one junction. 100 ft.

sheet-71-1.description: Sheet 71 is a small-scale sheet, drawn at 400 feet to an inch, covering the farmland of Shrewsbury Township that lies between the separately mapped built-up areas of Red Bank, Little Silver and Shrewsbury. It reaches from Pinkney Road at the top, on the edge of Red Bank, south across White Road and Sycamore Avenue to Parkers Creek and the Shrewsbury Township and Eatontown Township boundary at the bottom. Branch Avenue runs down the north-east side of the sheet past Rumson Road and Markham Road to the Little Silver station, where it meets Sycamore Avenue, Willow Drive, Eastview Avenue and Oceanport Avenue at the crossing of the New York and Long Branch Railroad, which cuts diagonally across the sheet. Coloured bands along the edges mark the limits of the larger-scale sheets that adjoin it (28, 32, 45, 46, 47, 49, 58, 60, 61 and 62), whose areas are left largely blank here. The land is divided into large numbered farm lots with scattered dwellings, barns, greenhouses and garages. Named holdings include the Swallowdale Squab Farm near Pinkney Road, H. L. Powers and the Shrewsbury Manor Tea Room on Sycamore Avenue, W. S. Fanshaw's Silver Brook Farm, Mrs. Carson Peck, K. S. Kodama, and the extensive greenhouses of Dean and Co., florists, near Little Silver station, for which the sheet refers to enlarged plans on sheet 46. Several brooks run east across the sheet to Parkers Creek. Water pipes are shown along Branch Avenue and parts of White Road and Sycamore Avenue. A small inset in the bottom right corner, at the same scale, continues the township boundary along the creek and is not georeferenced.
notes: Placed from four points (two detected, two hand-picked) at 400 ft to an inch; low confidence, a few metres to about 10 m.
Rumson Road and Markham Road meet Branch Avenue at spacings that do not match the modern Rumson Road and Markham Place junctions, so they were not used.
Pinkney is the modern Pinckney Road.
The bottom-right inset (part 2) shows only the creek and the township boundary and has no control.

Shrewsbury Township, 400 ft to an inch: farmland between Red Bank, Little Silver and Shrewsbury (Pinkney Rd, White Rd, Branch Av, Sycamore Av). Two parts: main map (part 1) and an inset bottom right (part 2) with only Parkers Creek and the township line.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset bottom right: Shrewsbury / Eatontown Township line along a creek (no road or other feature shared with the modern data).
